Software Dev Engineer, Antenna Calibration, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

As a Software Engineer for antenna calibration, you will collaborate with systems architects, hardware engineering design teams & FW/SW design teams to bring up and test systems combining FPGA, firmware, RF, and networking functions and build advanced tools for the following:

Characterizing subsystems and systems related to antennas
Complex data storage
Hardware test automation
Firmware design and implementation
Application development
Design automation for 2D and 3D structures
Develop bring up tools and scripts for phased array systems

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

jobs.title: Sr Software Development Engineer, Nitro Card, Annapurna Labs, K2-US
jobs.description:
Annapurna Labs (our organization within AWS UC) designs silicon and software that accelerates innovation. Customers choose us to create cloud solutions that solve challenges that were unimaginable a short time ago. Our custom chips, accelerators, and software stacks enable us to take on technical challenges that have never been seen before, and deliver results that help our customers change the world.

AWS Nitro is the underlying platform for our next generation EC2 instances. Comprised of custom AWS hardware and software that work together to deliver security and performance that is indistinguishable from bare metal.

As part of the Nitro team, you will be a thought leader supporting the ground-up development of key features that will support advanced hardware that offloads and accelerates IO for functions, security chips that enable the most secure cloud platform available today.

Key job responsibilities
Actively contribute to software development across all verticals, from Linux services and drivers, and related applications, Nitro card integration and Platform bringups.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to align development efforts with broader organizational goals.
Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends related to Nitro Cards and AWS infrastructure.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.

jobs.title: 2027 Software Dev Engineer Intern - Finland
jobs.description:
Please note the role is available across multiple locations in Germany.

Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands.

Our Software Development Engineer (SDE) interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As an SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers.

We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth.

Amazon internships across all seasons are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work in office, Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day. Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.

Key job responsibilities
Collaborate and communicate effectively with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to design, build, and operate innovative products and services that delight our customers, while participating in technical discussions to drive solutions forward.

Break down complex, ambiguous problems into well-defined, solvable components before implementation.

Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services, with distributed-systems scope varying by team.

Participate in code reviews as a core engineering practice, providing constructive feedback and validating correctness.

Contribute to clear and accurate technical documentation.

Use GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity, and critically validate, verify, and integrate AI-generated code, exercising sound judgement about when to trust AI output.

Write clean, maintainable code following best practices and design patterns.

Work in an agile environment practicing CI/CD principles while participating in operational responsibilities including on-call duties.

Demonstrate operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, and resolving production issues.

A day in the life
As an intern, you will be matched to a manager and a mentor and will have the opportunity to influence the evolution of Amazon technology and lead critical projects early in your career.

In addition to working on an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage with Amazonians for both personal and professional development, expand your network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship. No matter the location of your internship, we give you the tools to own your project and learn in a real-world setting.

About the team

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, AWS Distributed SQL
jobs.description:
AWS Databases is hiring Principal/Sr Principal Engineers to lead query processing for two of its key database engines. Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse used by tens of thousands of customers. Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for active-active availability and virtually unlimited scale. Both engines depend on the same discipline: turning SQL into well-optimized plans and running them fast at massive scale. Depending on your depth and interests, you'll join one of three teams: Redshift Query Optimization, the Redshift Execution Engine, or Aurora DSQL Query Processing.

Key job responsibilities
- Set and execute a multi-year technical strategy for query optimization and execution that improves price-performance against Databricks, Snowflake, Google BigQuery, and other cloud databases.
- Own core query processing architecture, including parsing and semantic analysis, query rewriting, cost-based planning, statistics and cardinality estimation, plan caching, and physical execution.
- Build high-performance execution engines (vectorized and pipelined operators, memory management, code generation, massively parallel and distributed execution) that serve analytical and transactional workloads.
- Advance optimization over open table formats and heterogeneous storage, such as Iceberg and Parquet data lakes and federated sources. Build adaptive execution that corrects plans at runtime.
- Turn ambiguous customer and business requirements into concrete projects, and personally own design, code, deployment, and operations from end to end.
- Partner across AWS Databases on product vision and integration with the broader database portfolio. Work directly with customers on adoption and roadmap.
- Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, coding standards, and operational excellence. Mentor senior engineers, and help hire and grow a strong team.

We make AWS billing data trustworthy at the source. As a Software Development Engineer II on the Billing Data Services (BiDS) team, you will build and operate the foundational systems that capture, store, and serve the billing facts that AWS billing services rely on.

Our services sit upstream of bill computation systems. We ingest billing data from across AWS (such as pricing, subscriptions, and entitlements), persist it as a single source of truth, and serve it to the teams and pipelines that join it with usage to synthesize customer-facing billing artifacts. We operate at the scale of all of AWS, where correctness is non-negotiable and a single bad record can ripple into thousands of customer bills.

As a software engineer on this team, you will develop and improve large-scale distributed systems built on AWS services. You will learn new technologies, design durable storage and serving paths, and build the data layer that hundreds of AWS teams depend on. Your work will impact millions of external customers and sit on the critical path of Billing.

Key job responsibilities
- Write high-quality, efficient, and testable code in Java and other object-oriented languages.
- Build large-scale, highly available distributed systems for ingesting, storing, and serving authoritative billing data at the scale of all of AWS.
- Design storage and serving paths that meet demanding freshness, accuracy, and latency requirements for downstream billing pipelines.
- Partner with downstream teams on schema and data contract changes, making sure migrations are backward compatible and do not disrupt their pipelines.
- Own and operate the systems you build, holding a high bar for data quality, correctness, and operational rigor.
- Contribute to planning, design, implementation, testing, operations, and process improvement as a member of a Scrum team.
- Collaborate with product managers and engineers across Commerce Platform teams to deliver features and drive the adoption of best practices.

A day in the life
You might start the morning reviewing ingestion and data quality dashboards before joining a design review for a new storage or serving path. By midday, you are working with a downstream team on a schema or data contract change, making sure the migration is backward compatible and won't disrupt their pipelines. In the afternoon, you are deep in an approach to cut serving latency or raise ingestion throughput, then aligning with a partner team on an upstream event format change. You balance long-term platform investments with the immediate needs of the teams that depend on your data.

About the team
We own the systems that hold and serve the authoritative billing facts for AWS Commerce Platform services. BiDS delivers timely and consistent operational billing data to support near real-time bill computation and cost and usage monitoring for AWS, giving billing teams a high-performance, queryable, and cost-effective data layer to store and access operational billing data.

Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, built to deliver fast, reliable broadband to customers and communities around the world, including places traditional networks don't reach.

As a Software Development Engineer II on the Leo Ground Control Console team, you'll build the services, infrastructure and platform that power the web tools Leo's engineers and operators use every day to run the constellation. That includes mission operations, network health, satellite and ground systems, and leadership views of network performance. You'll own systems end to end, from design and infrastructure as code through production operations.

What you'll do
- Design and build backend services and APIs that connect operator tools to data and systems across Leo's ground and space segments, with a focus on security, reliability and low latency.
- Own the cloud infrastructure behind a shared platform used by many teams: infrastructure as code, deployment pipelines, account and access guardrails, and the shared constructs other teams build on.
- Make the platform fast and dependable at fleet scale. Find where latency and errors come from across services, fix them, and prove the improvement with data.
- Build in observability: metrics, alarms, logging and real-user monitoring, so problems surface before users report them.
- Work with engineering teams across ground and space systems to turn complex mission workflows into robust, well-designed systems.
- Raise the bar on engineering practice: design reviews, automated code review and quality checks, safe deployments, and AI-assisted development workflows that help a small team move quickly without lowering the bar.
- Support high-stakes moments such as launches, on-orbit operations and operational rehearsals, where the systems have to just work.

About you
You care about craft, reliability and the people who depend on what you build. You're comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end, balancing several priorities, and staying calm under pressure. You have strong software engineering fundamentals, experience building and operating distributed systems or cloud services, and you like making complex systems simpler and faster. Experience with infrastructure as code, security, performance tuning or frontend platforms is a plus. Familiarity with space or network systems is welcome but not required; you'll learn the domain here.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

About the team
The Leo Ground Control Console team owns the operational tooling used across Amazon Leo, on the ground and in orbit. We build a shared platform that is scalable, reliable, adaptable and fast, so every team at Leo can deliver tools their users rely on. We're a small, high-ownership team that ships quickly, measures its impact, and invests in the tools and practices that make the whole organization more productive.

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test and operate backend services, APIs and infrastructure for Amazon Leo's operator and leadership tools, from design through production support.
- Own the platform's cloud infrastructure and deployment pipelines as code, including the shared building blocks and guardrails other teams depend on.
- Measure and improve the latency, reliability and cost of services and their dependencies, and make them resilient to slow or failing systems.
- Add metrics, alarms and logging to what you ship, and use the data to prioritize improvements and show their impact.
- Partner with engineers, operators and product owners across ground and space systems to understand requirements and turn them into well-designed solutions.
- Write high-quality, well-tested code, review others' changes, and help define the team's design standards, security practices and automated quality checks.
- Improve developer productivity through better tooling, CI/CD, test automation and AI-assisted development workflows.
- Participate in on-call and support launches, on-orbit operations and operational rehearsals.

About the team
The Ground Control Console team owns the operational tooling platform used across Project Leo to support all aspects of the mission, both on the ground and in orbit. We prioritize building a platform that is scalable, reliable, adaptable and performant in order to provide our customers with tools and support that they have come to rely on for the mission's ongoing success.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AI Foundations, Amazon Leo Networking Software
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's Low Earth Orbit satellite network, built to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. The AI Foundations team builds AI agents that turn Leo's best troubleshooting expertise into diagnoses in minutes instead of hours, helping keep the network available for every customer.

As a Software Development Engineer on AI Foundations, you will design and build production agentic systems on AWS that reason over real satellite, ground, and network data. You will work directly with principal engineers and network operators, and your work will shape how Leo is operated at scale.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate AI agents and services that diagnose network and connectivity issues using telemetry, logs, and engineering knowledge.
- Turn proven engineering tools and data sources into reusable agent tools so teams across Leo can build on them.
- Build evaluation harnesses that measure agent accuracy, coverage, and latency, and use them to gate launches.
- Own your services in production: on-call, operational metrics, root-cause analysis, and security reviews.
- Partner with principal engineers, operators, and program managers to turn ambiguous problems into shipped features.
- Write clear design docs, give thoughtful code reviews, and help teammates adopt agentic development practices.

A day in the life
You might start the morning reviewing overnight evaluation results and spotting a class of network failures your agent misdiagnosed. You trace the gap to a missing data source, then sit down with the principal engineer who owns that subsystem to agree on how to expose their tool to the agent. After lunch you build the integration and add new test cases, then review a teammate's pull request. Late afternoon, you join an operations review where an operator walks through a real incident your agent helped resolve, and you leave with a clear next priority.

About the team
AI Foundations is a new team in Amazon Leo's networking software organization. Our mission is to help Leo reach and sustain its network availability goals by turning the organization's best troubleshooting expertise into AI agents anyone can use. We build the shared foundations (agent tooling, evaluation, and integrations) that let engineering and operations teams across Leo ship their own agents safely. Because the team is early, you will help shape its architecture, engineering bar, and culture. We value builders who are curious about how satellite networks work, measure what they ship, and prefer simple systems that operators trust.

jobs.title: Software Development Manager, Amazon Customer Service
jobs.description:
We see our customers as invited guests to a party, and we are the hosts. It's our job every day to make every important aspect of the customer experience a little bit better." - Jeff Bezos, Founder & CEO

We didn’t make Amazon a trillion-dollar company, our customers did, and we want to ensure that our customers always have a positive experience that keeps them coming back to Amazon. To help achieve this, the Customer Experience Improvement (CXI) team, within Amazon Customer Service (CS), relentlessly focuses on maintaining customer trust by building products that offer appropriate resolutions to resolve issues faced by our customers. CXI engineers solve complex problems and build scalable, robust solutions to help our customers navigate through issues and eliminate systemic defects to prevent future issues and identify critical customer experience improvement opportunities. This role will leverage latest technologies and Agentic AI solutions to autonomously eliminate defects at scale to improve customer experience.


Key job responsibilities
- Lead a team of SDEs that create and own scalable solutions that empower Amazon to deliver a defect-free experience for customers.
- Grow existing talent and hire new talent to quickly scale the platform to accelerate defect elimination across Amazon.
- Tackle complex technical challenges, create innovative solutions with direct impact on customer trust, and work on systems critical to Amazon's operational excellence.

About the team
ARCADE (Automated Root Causing, Attribution and Defect Elimination) is the Defect Elimination system within CXI Tech, manifesting Amazon's commitment to preventing customers from receiving defective products that degrade their experience. ARCADE leverages AI to transform how we detect repeat negative customer experiences and eliminate the underlying upstream defects at scale. The CXI Tech team re-imagines how we leverage customer interactions and feedback — through modular capabilities spanning Detection, Triage, Root Cause, Attribution, and Resolution — to enable more reliable and faster defect elimination that drives customer experience improvements throughout the consumer business. The system combines associate-driven signals (empowering front-line CSAs to flag product problems) with statistical and machine learning-based automated detection, intelligent prioritization, and increasingly autonomous investigation through our agentic ecosystem. ARCADE serves multiple tenants including Andon Cords (high-severity defects) and customer service quality, providing a unified, scalable approach to defect elimination across Amazon.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Data Center Builder Tools
jobs.description:
The Data Center Builder Tools team is looking for a seasoned, self-directed Software Development Engineer (SDE II) to help define AWS next generation real-time middleware and controls platform that powers industrial control systems across AWS Data Centers worldwide. Contribute to Amazon's vision of developing the safest, most secure, reliable, and efficient data centers on Earth.

As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will set the technical direction for the software that sits between industrial hardware and the cloud, a unified, real-time data plane that lets control applications, device drivers, and cloud services exchange data reliably on industrial computing hardware. This is deep systems work at the boundary of software and hardware: you will own the architecture of the controls, the communication layer, and the protocol and cloud integrations that the entire platform is built on, and you will be the engineer others turn to for the hardest problems in real-time, distributed, and embedded systems.

Key job responsibilities
As an SDE II on this team, you are a technical leader accountable for the architecture and long-term health of the controls and middleware platform, not just individual components. You will operate across multiple workstreams and teams, make the consequential design decisions, and remain deeply hands-on where it matters most.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

* Architecting the platform, not just components: owning the end-to-end design of the controls and real-time middleware across embedded/edge controllers and the cloud, making the durable decisions on type systems, serialization, memory layout, schema evolution, and communication patterns that everything else depends on.

* Owning real-time correctness at system scale: reasoning about latency budgets, throughput, determinism, and failure modes across a distributed system adjacent to physical control loops, and setting the standards that keep those guarantees intact as the system grows.

* Raising the engineering bar broadly: establishing standards for testing (unit, integration, and on-hardware validation), performance benchmarking, operational excellence, and code quality, and holding the team to them through design and code review.

* Growing engineers: mentoring Junior SDEs, developing their technical judgment, and contributing as a strong interviewer and bar raiser in hiring.

* De-risking the hardest problems: personally diving into the highest-ambiguity, highest-impact technical challenges (new protocol integrations, performance-critical paths, cross-language data exchange) and bringing them to a proven, maintainable end state.

The ideal candidate is a software engineer with a track record of owning the architecture of complex software systems and delivering them to production. jobs.title: Software Development Manager, Amazon Software Builder Experience - Change Review, Amazon Software Builder Experience – Change Auto Review Experience (CRUX)
jobs.description:
Are you an engineering leader who wants to shape how software changes are reviewed and merged in the era of AI? The Change Review team within Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) builds the tools and services that help Amazon engineering teams review and ship software changes safely and confidently.

AI-assisted development is changing the volume and nature of software changes and increasing the importance of reliable review and merge workflows. We are looking for a Software Development Manager to lead a team building automated verification, publication, queuing, and merge capabilities. You will build and develop the team, own its technical and delivery roadmap in partnership with product leadership, and operate reliable systems that help builders advance changes safely and efficiently.

This role combines people leadership, technical depth, execution, and operational ownership. You will work backwards from builders, make decisions in an ambiguous and fast-changing domain, align partner teams, and maintain a high quality and reliability bar for the services your team delivers.

Key job responsibilities
Hire, develop, coach, and retain a diverse team of software engineers; establish clear expectations and help engineers grow their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.
Own the team's technical and delivery roadmap in partnership with product leadership, translating customer priorities into executable plans and clear engineering outcomes.
Lead the design, delivery, operation, and continuous improvement of automated verification, publication, queuing, and merge services.
Establish mechanisms for predictable execution, dependency management, technical reviews, launch readiness, operational health, and durable follow-through.
Partner with product managers, senior engineers, customers, and dependent teams to resolve ambiguity, make trade-offs, and align interfaces and priorities.
Maintain a high technical and operational bar across architecture, security, correctness, reliability, maintainability, testing, observability, and incident response.
Establish responsible AI-assisted engineering practices in which engineers direct and validate AI tools while retaining clear human ownership of every design and production change.
Use customer feedback, operational signals, and engineering data to evaluate outcomes and improve product, delivery, and operational mechanisms.
Create an inclusive team environment that encourages constructive challenge, collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning.

A day in the life
Your day might begin with an operational or delivery review where you help the team understand a reliability issue, resolve a dependency, or make a technical trade-off. You may then coach an engineer, review the design of a verification or merge workflow, align a delivery plan with product leadership, or work with a partner team on an integration.

You will balance people development, technical judgment, execution, and operations. As AI-assisted development evolves, you will help the team build dependable mechanisms for reviewing and advancing software changes while keeping quality, safety, and accountable human judgment at the center.

About the team
Amazon Software Builder Experience creates tools and services that help Amazon engineering teams build, review, and deliver software. The Change Review team focuses on making software changes easier to understand, safer to review, and more dependable to merge.

We are shaping the future of change review as AI-assisted software development evolves. We value customer focus, sound engineering judgment, collaboration, technical craftsmanship, operational excellence, and inclusive leadership. We invest in our engineers' growth and expect managers to create an environment where people can do their best work and every perspective is heard.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, Programming Foundations
jobs.description:
Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX), started in 2022, is working to make Amazon the best place to build software. One of our most important responsibilities is shaping the language ecosystem, both inside Amazon and across the open-source community, to improve the experience for every software builder.

Our tools are used in all aspects of the business, and their care and evolution are of critical importance to the effectiveness of Amazon. We're looking for a deeply technical leader interested in sustaining and evolving the shared software platform used by nearly every service within the company. Those with experience evolving broadly distributed and highly complex software libraries, such as large open source projects and mission critical foundational software stacks will be given an opportunity to have company wide impact.

Key job responsibilities
You will design and build developer tools that Amazon engineers use every day. You will work with the languages and libraries that power Amazon's services, making them easier to use and more reliable. You will help maintain our build tools, compilers, libraries and frameworks. You will shape how OSS upstream projects are developing, including contributing to them directly yourself. You will collaborate with engineers across Amazon to understand their pain points and build tools, libraries and frameworks that address them. You will write code, review code from teammates, and help others debug issues with our tools.

Your work will directly affect how builders at Amazon do their jobs. We are a language expertise team at the heart of being able to compile and shift software. This is practical work that requires understanding what builders actually need and building tools that solve their problems without getting in the way.



About the team
The Language Experience team has 3 primary missions. Language toolchains supporting the compiler, package managers, and build tools themselves enabling builders to do their job. Supply chain security and ingestion for 3rd party packages making open source software available to builders in a timely and secure manner. Providing the best developer experience in each support programming language through improvements directly on the language and key packages both inside the company and upstream in open source.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Leo Live
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Developer Experience organization owns the entire path from commit to satellite. This is a unique opportunity to offer this scope to platform engineers.
We will build a unified platform that empower Leo engineers to see their code affect satellite operations within days not weeks, months or a quarter. We will build a self-service platform as the intelligence layer, to empower engineers with real-time root cause attribution and triaging in CT production, conversational analytics agents, automated narrative generation and potential bugs discovery capabilities.

We are looking for a engineer with experience in supporting mission-critical applications, who are excited about building solutions that enhance automation, stability, and release processes across multiple systems.
You will be the technical anchor for how the system will be built from ground up. You bring strong depth in distributed systems, knowledge representation, and AI/ML engineering, combined with the people leadership skills to hire, develop, and retain high-performing engineers in a fast-moving, ambiguous domain.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
A successful engineer in this role is :
- Highly analytical: You solve problems in ways that can be backed up with verifiable data. You focus on driving processes, tools, and statistical methods which support rational decision-making.
- Technically fearless: You aren't satisfied by performing 'as expected' and push the limits past conventional boundaries. Your dial goes to '11'.
- Team obsessed: You help grow your team members to achieve outstanding results. You foster the creative atmosphere to let engineers innovate, while holding them accountable for making smart decisions and delivering results.
- You’re ambitious, yet humble: You recognize that there’s always opportunity for improvement and use introspection and feedback from teammates and peers to raise the bar for your team.
- Engaged by ambiguity: You're able to explore new problem spaces with unique constraints and thus non-obvious solutions; you’re quick to identify any gaps in the team and the right person to fill them to best deliver value to customers.
- Own technical vision and direction: You identify problems and develop solutions; you embrace performance metrics and measurement techniques because they help you assess how well system-related services are running.
- Build and grow your team: You'll be a key contributor on an engineering team that delivers results.
- Invent and simplify: You will apply the first principal thinking into your work and find a simple solution to tackle the fundamental problem.

A day in the life
A Software Development Engineer works closely with Principal Engineer, Sr. Principal Engineer to deal with ambiguity and define technical strategy. The engineer will also work with the release teams to deeply understand the current workflow, use cases, pain points, inefficiency and come up with innovative simple solution.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AIO Visualization and Reporting
jobs.description:
Join a team that builds the experiences every AWS customer uses to understand, monitor, and optimize what they spend, from individual developers to enterprise FinOps teams managing tens of millions of dollars in monthly spend. The AWS Billing Console Platform team owns the console's hosting platform, on which around thirty AWS engineering teams build their console pages; over fifty customer-facing billing and cost pages of its own; and the rendering engine that turns an AI agent's cost data into the charts, tables and reports customers see.

Two AWS agents answer cost questions today, a FinOps agent and Amazon Q in the console, and chatbots and console pages form one ecosystem customers navigate between to get problems solved and questions answered. Today each renders its answers its own way, and a cost figure has to be right the first time. This team is building the rendering layer both agents will draw on: an engine that checks every plotted value against the data the agent gathered, an open artifact format any agent host can render, and the component catalog that makes a cost chart look the same wherever it appears.

We are hiring a Software Development Engineer to extend this rendering platform to provide effective visualization for any problem that our web pages handle, especially for risky mutative actions. You'll use only the latest genAI, open source and proprietary technologies to directly enhance agents to give them the power of our AWS management console pages for problems that can only be solved visually or that require supervision by users.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test, and operate the rendering engine behind AWS's cost agents: the components, the emit path, and the checks that verify every number before a customer sees it.
- Bring generated cost visualizations into agent conversations against the accuracy and customer-outcome bars the team sets, and keep two agent hosts rendering the same artifact from the same data.
- Define and publish a rendering format for cost artifacts and adopt the open protocol the console ecosystem is converging on.
- Build and operate customer-facing console pages on the team's page-building platform and component library.
- Help scale a platform that absorbed the work of three teams in a 2026 reorganization: drive down operational load through automation, observability, and legacy-service decommissioning so the team can invest in new customer experiences.
- Own services end to end, including participation in the team's on-call rotation for production support.
- Raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, automated evaluation, and operational excellence, and partner with product managers, applied scientists, designers, and the agent teams across AWS.

A day in the life
You start by checking the health of the services you own and clearing anything handed off from on-call, then pick up your current project: maybe a new artifact type, where you run the agent's answers through the team's fidelity scorecard, read where a figure drifted from its source, and fix the emit path. Midday you review a teammate's component, then join a design review where the team and the agent teams weigh how one artifact renders in two hosts. In the afternoon you pair with an applied scientist on the evaluation set for the next release and sketch the components a new chart needs. Across the week you balance net-new rendering and platform work against the operational excellence that billing customers depend on, and rotate through on-call. The problems are open-ended, the customer scale is large, and the design space is new, so there is room to set technical direction and take on new scope. You will have the support of an experienced team and a manager invested in your growth.

About the team
The AWS Billing Console Platform team owns the platform, the customer-facing pages, and the rendering engine that AWS customers and AWS's cost agents use to manage cloud spend. We operate at scale. Around thirty AWS engineering teams build their console pages on our hosting platform, which gains two to three new console pages every year, and we own over fifty customer-facing pages ourselves, with a production footprint consolidated from three teams in a 2026 reorganization and driven toward lower operational load through automation and legacy-service decommissioning. We own generative UI for billing and cost management, the rendering engine the FinOps agent runs in production and the cost-visualization skill Amazon Q is launching, and we are extending that ownership into a platform: the agent interfaces, the generated experiences, and the open format customers will see across AWS's cost agents. That combination, a large operational platform plus a green-field AI mandate, means an engineer here can take on scope quickly and see a clear path to the next level. We operate what we build, hold a high bar for operational excellence, and care about inclusion, mentorship, and work-life harmony, so engineers at every level can do their best work and grow their careers.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Sponsored Products and Brands

These predictions decide which ads are relevant, how they rank, and how advertisers get value.

Our team builds and runs the ML infrastructure behind those models, end to end:

- Offline feature engineering: a multi-tenant platform used by several ML teams. It runs thousands of daily feature jobs over petabyte-scale data and produces the features that train models in every marketplace we serve.
- Model training: the standard system that retrains CTR and CVR models every day. How fresh these models are directly affects advertiser results and Amazon's revenue.
- Online feature store and feature retrieval: low-latency, high-throughput services that provide features when a model makes a prediction. These predictions feed the scores used in real-time ad ranking.
- Next-generation research platform: a platform that uses AI agents to help scientists explore, test and launch new model ideas faster.

As an SDE II, you'll design, build and run distributed systems that work at very large scale, both in offline batch processing and online serving. You'll work closely with applied scientists and engineers to make models fresher, help scientists try ideas faster, and keep the systems that support ads ranking reliable.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop ML infrastructure for advanced recommendation models, from training through real-time inference, that delivers highly relevant ads to shoppers worldwide
- Improve the scalability, automation and efficiency of large-scale training and real-time inference systems
- Work closely with applied scientists to optimize the performance of ML models and infrastructure, and take models from experimentation into production
- Deliver ML solutions end to end: design, implementation, testing, deployment and operations
- Collaborate with engineers and scientists across the team to build systems that serve ads across all Amazon platforms and surfaces
- Participate in design and code reviews and mentor peers

A day in the life
You might start the day checking the health of the overnight feature and training pipelines. Then you'd work with scientists on how to support a new model architecture, and spend the afternoon building a performance improvement for the online feature store. You'll ship often, see your work affect ads served around the world, and influence how ML infrastructure grows across the organization.

About the team
The Sponsored Products and Brands team at Amazon Ads is re-imagining the advertising landscape through industry leading generative AI technologies, revolutionizing how millions of customers discover products and engage with brands across Amazon.com and beyond. We are at the forefront of re-inventing advertising experiences, bridging human creativity with artificial intelligence to transform every aspect of the advertising lifecycle from ad creation and optimization to performance analysis and customer insights. We value ownership, getting things done, and close collaboration with science partners. We invest in mentorship and in tools that make engineers and scientists more productive, including AI-assisted development.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - Network Observability, Leo Networking Software
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s Low Earth Orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team builds the systems that provide deep, end-to-end insight into the health, performance, and reliability of this global telecom network. Our systems span the full Leo service—from satellites and customer terminals to ground gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial network infrastructure—and enable engineers to understand network behavior, rapidly detect failures, and diagnose complex issues across space and ground infrastructure.
We are looking for a talented Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate network observability and analytics solutions for an advanced global telecommunications service spanning both space and terrestrial networks.

As a software engineer on this team, you will build high-scale systems that transform telemetry, network events, traces, and operational signals into actionable visibility. You will work across distributed systems, networking, data pipelines, real-time analytics, and visualization to answer critical questions such as: Is the network healthy? Where is a failure occurring? What is its customer impact? And how quickly can we identify and resolve it?
You will collaborate closely with network engineers, scientists, and software engineers to develop novel mechanisms for end-to-end network visibility and diagnostics. Your work will help establish the observability foundations required to operate a highly distributed telecom network where failures can span satellites, beams, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop highly scalable network observability, telemetry, and analytics systems spanning space and terrestrial infrastructure.
- Build real-time and near-real-time pipelines that ingest and correlate high-volume network telemetry, events, traces, and health signals.
- Develop algorithms and services that provide end-to-end network visibility, including failure detection, localization, correlation, and impact analysis.
- Build tools and platforms that enable engineers to quickly understand network health and diagnose complex, multi-hop failures.
- Design distributed systems capable of processing large volumes of telemetry while maintaining high availability, durability, and low latency.
- Develop APIs, services, dashboards, and analytical tools that expose network health and operational insights to internal customers.
- Work closely with network engineers and scientists to translate complex networking problems into robust software solutions.
- Establish metrics, service-level indicators, and automated detection mechanisms for critical Leo network components.
- Design systems that remain resilient in the presence of intermittent connectivity, partial failures, delayed telemetry, and unreliable network paths.
- Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support.
- Drive technical decisions across team boundaries and contribute to engineering standards for observability, reliability, and operational excellence.
- Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software development.


A day in the life
You will work on problems at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, telemetry, and large-scale analytics. One day you might design a streaming architecture capable of processing telemetry from millions of network components; another day you might develop a mechanism to identify where packet loss occurred across a multi-hop satellite and terrestrial path.
You will work with network engineers and scientists to understand how Leo’s network behaves, develop new ways to make that behavior observable, and turn large volumes of operational data into actionable information. You will also own services in production and work through real operational challenges as the network scales.
This role provides opportunities to work across the stack—from telemetry collection on network infrastructure and embedded systems, through distributed data pipelines and analytics, to the APIs and visualization tools used by engineers operating the Leo network.



About the team
The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team is responsible for making a highly distributed global telecom network understandable and operable at scale.
We build the visibility layer that connects network signals across satellites, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure. Our systems help transform individual telemetry signals into an end-to-end view of network health, enabling faster detection, diagnosis, and resolution of issues.
The problems we solve are inherently distributed and require us to combine software engineering with networking and data science. We are building new capabilities rather than simply applying existing observability patterns to a conventional cloud service.
If you enjoy solving ambiguous problems, designing distributed systems at significant scale, and building software that provides visibility into complex networks, this team offers an opportunity to work on foundational systems for Amazon Leo.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, SoC HAL
jobs.description:
Description

Annapurna Labs builds the custom silicon at the heart of AWS machine learning servers, and we are hiring a software engineer to help build the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) that brings these chips to life. If you love working where hardware meets software, writing the code that boots, configures, and debugs some of the largest custom silicon in the world, this is your team.

As a Software Engineer on the SoC HAL team, you will write and test C++ for the driver stack across the hardware blocks that make up our chips, learn how the silicon works from the engineers who design it, and grow your skills on a small, fast-moving team inside a large organization. No machine learning background is required (you will pick up ML concepts from colleagues if you want to). This role is based in Cupertino, CA.

Key job responsibilities
Implement, test, and maintain HAL/driver features for individual hardware blocks (for example PCIe, DDR / HBM memory, DMA, system fabric, interrupt controllers, and boot / firmware), working from designs and interfaces set by more senior engineers.

Write clean, well-tested C++ and contribute to the team's test, code-review, and continuous-deployment practices.

Debug failures that span software and silicon, with support from the team, and build an understanding of how the HAL interacts with the hardware underneath it.

Learn the hardware/software interface by partnering with RTL and design verification engineers on well-scoped questions.

Provide feature additions and bug fixes on current and prior chips.

A day in the life
A typical day moves between writing and reviewing C++ for the HAL, pairing with a teammate on a tricky bug, and learning how a hardware block works from its spec or from the engineer who designed it. You might add a feature to a driver, write tests for it, and work through code-review feedback, then dig into a failure that spans software and silicon. Your teammates are the HAL engineers you build alongside; the hardware design, verification, and firmware teams are close partners you will learn from; and your customers are the internal software teams that rely on the HAL to boot, configure, and debug the chip.

About the team
Annapurna Labs designs and deploys some of the largest custom silicon in the world, including the Trainium and Inferentia machine learning accelerators. Our SoC HAL team builds the low-level software that boots, configures, and manages these chips, sitting between the hardware and the system software that runs the server. We are a small team that works closely with hardware, holds a high engineering bar, and invests in helping engineers grow. Based in Cupertino, CA, we value mentorship, clear written design, and software that outlasts any single chip.

jobs.description:

We are on a bold mission to reimagine how the internet's edge operates at planetary scale — building the Border Network of the future: software-defined, running on commodity hardware, and programmable at every layer. Catographer will act as the brain of the network, continuously ingesting real-time signals such as routing information to determine how traffic should flow across Amazon's global border network. It translates those decisions into directives for the underlying network controllers, enabling fast and reliable traffic management at massive scale. By replacing legacy routing approaches with a modern, horizontally scalable platform built in Rust, Catographer improves network reliability, reduces the blast radius of failures, and unlocks advanced traffic engineering capabilities — all while handling network state changes in milliseconds. This is a unique opportunity to work on a foundational platform for how traffic enters and exits Amazon's network.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Antenna Team
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo Antenna team is looking for a Software Development Engineer who is excited to work at the intersection of large-scale data systems, Amazon Web Services cloud services, data analysis, and radio frequency hardware.

In this role, you will design and build Customer Terminal Fleet Health, the system that keeps a daily hardware health record for every customer terminal Leo operates and flags terminals whose hardware is starting to fail. You will turn telemetry from millions of satellite contacts a day into clear, trustworthy signals that tell engineers which terminals need attention and why. You do not need to come in as a radio frequency expert, but you should have a strong software engineering foundation, experience building data pipelines on Amazon Web Services, a high learning velocity, and the drive to understand phased array antennas, satellite links, and how hardware failures show up in telemetry.

This is an individual contributor software development role for someone who enjoys ambiguous technical problems, can learn across disciplines, and wants to build data systems that directly improve the reliability of a satellite network.

Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
Design and build data pipelines on AWS (Step Functions, Athena, Glue, Iceberg, Lambda, S3) that process daily telemetry for the full fleet of customer terminals.
Define and own the data model for fleet health: daily per-terminal aggregates, per-satellite views, and the history engineers use to investigate a single terminal.
Partner with RF and antenna engineers to understand signal quality, temperature, reboot, and link metrics well enough to separate hardware failures from network, weather, and satellite effects.
Develop and validate the rules and models that flag failing hardware, and measure how well they work against terminals returned for repair.
Build infrastructure as code with AWS CDK, with deployment pipelines, monitoring, alarms, and integration tests that keep the system reliable.
Build dashboards and tools that let engineering and operations teams explore fleet health, compare groups of terminals, and track the effect of software and hardware changes.
Apply strong security and data-handling practices to sensitive customer and device data, including least-privilege access, encryption, and privacy controls.
Collaborate with data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard new data sources and improve the telemetry the system depends on.
Write high-quality, maintainable code and documentation that other engineers and teams across Leo can build on.

A day in the life
You may start the day reviewing the overnight fleet health run, checking that every data source arrived and looking at which terminals were newly flagged. You might then sit down with antenna and radio frequency engineers on a group of terminals whose signal quality dropped, digging through the data together to decide whether it points to failing hardware, a software release, or something outside the terminal.

Later, you may meet with the data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard a new telemetry source, then write the infrastructure and pipeline code that brings it into the daily run with tests and alarms in place. You might finish the day with field operations, comparing the watch list against recent hardware returns to see which failures the system flagged early, which it missed, and what each returned terminal can teach the rules.

Across all of it, your work helps engineers spot failing hardware before customers notice and measure the effect of software and hardware changes across the fleet. This role requires curiosity, technical depth, and the ability to move between data engineering, cloud infrastructure, and hardware context. You will not just write code; you will help define how Leo understands the health of every terminal in its fleet.

About the team
The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect customers to the Leo satellite network. We provide embedded application software and the underlying Linux system software for these terminals. We work hand in hand with hardware, product, and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers. As Leo moves toward full-scale production and global deployment, this is a compelling time to join and help shape how millions of people get online for the first time.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and own tier-1 services that determine ad-serving eligibility across Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display
- Build global, auto-scalable, high-throughput services that work across all ad programs — from campaign management through event logging
- Collaborate with software engineers, scientists, Product Managers, and Program Managers to deliver compelling advertiser and customer experiences

The Sponsored Products and Brands team at Amazon Ads is re-imagining the advertising landscape through industry leading generative AI technologies, revolutionizing how millions of customers discover products and engage with brands across Amazon.com and beyond. If you're energized by solving complex challenges and pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AI, join us in shaping the future of advertising.

jobs.title: Software Development Manager
jobs.description:
Project Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

In this role, you will develop software for the Leo Customer Terminal embedded systems engineering team. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, deployment and operations of the functions for Leo Customer Terminals.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.





Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
* Development and testing with embedded Linux
* Develop embedded software functions for Customer Terminal devices within the Project Leo system
* Developing embedded software utilizing Rust, C++, C
* Participate in all phases of SDLC: requirements, design, coding, test, deployment and production system
* Development of software in a secure compute environment
* State machine design and analysis
* Support Customer Terminal deployments operations and debugging on production systems
* Technical writing of design specifications

A day in the life

As part of our software engineering team, you will lead a team of embedded software developers, and design software for Leo Customer Terminal platforms in R&D and commercial operation. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams in Leo Customer Terminal hardware development, software development and operations. You need to be flexible and responsive to fast changing priorities and issues. You will work on Customer Terminal issues on production system platforms.

About the team

The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team develops and supports the devices that connect Leo subscribers to the Leo network. We provide software for the Leo Customer Terminal platform, applications and underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware engineering, product, and operations teams to deliver commercial grade services for our Leo subscribers.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer II, Business Data Technologies
jobs.description:
Amazon’s eCommerce Foundation (eCF) organization is responsible for the core components that drive the Amazon website and customer experience. Serving millions of customer page views and orders per day, eCF builds for scale. As an organization within eCF, the Business Data Technologies (BDT) group is no exception. We collect petabytes of data from thousands of data sources inside and outside Amazon including the Amazon catalog system, inventory system, customer order system, page views on the website and Alexa systems. We also support Amazon subsidiaries such as IMDB and Audible. We provide interfaces for our internal customers to access and query the data hundreds of thousands of times per day, using Amazon Web Service’s (AWS) Redshift, Hive, Spark, Scala and Flink. We build scalable solutions that grow with the Amazon business.
BDT is growing, and the data processing landscape is shifting. Our data is consumed by thousands of teams across Amazon including Research Scientists, Machine Learning Specialists, Business Analysts and Data Engineers. BDT team is building an enterprise-wide Data Lake leveraging AWS technologies. We enable teams at Amazon to produce analytical data in any form of storage (S3, DynamoDB, Aurora, etc.) and process that data using any type of compute environment such as EMR/Spark, Redshift, Athena, and others via a common bus. We are developing innovative products including the next-generation of data catalog, data discovery engine, data transformation platform, and more with state-of-the-art user experience. We’re looking for top engineers to build them from the ground up.
This is a hands-on position where you will do everything from designing and building extremely scalable components and cutting-edge features to formulating strategy and direction for data processing at Amazon. You will also mentor junior engineers and work with the most sophisticated customers in the business to help them get the best results. You need to not only be a top software developer with excellent programming skills, have an understanding of data processing and parallelization, and a stellar record of delivery, but also excel at leadership and customer obsession and have a real passion for massive-scale computing.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Keeping your finger on the pulse of the constantly evolving and growing data processing and data lake field
- Translation of complex functional and technical requirements into detailed architecture and design
- Delivering systems and features with top-notch quality, on time
- Stay current on technical knowledge to keep pace with rapidly changing technology, and work with the team in bringing new technologies on board

A day in the life

Work/Life Balance
Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility in working hours and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.
Mentorship & Career Growth
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded professional and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

Come help us build for the future of Data Lake!

A day in the life
The challenges SDEs solve for at Amazon are big and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products around the world. We are looking for individuals who are passionate about creating new products, features, and services from scratch while managing ambiguity and the pace of a company where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

About the team
Huron team under BDT owns the Streaming Ingestion Platform (DataCraft) with ~19K pipelines running actively on the platform and sinking data to Andes, S3 and EDX in micro batches using AWS Managed Flink infrastructure. We also work on improving the developer productivity areas including guidelines\recommendations of AI based operations and development practices.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, EC2 UltraServer Delivery Team
jobs.description:
The Software Development Engineer II will design, build, and maintain cloud-based provisioning workflows for NVIDIA GB200/GB300 UltraServers, orchestrating complex multi-asset systems from infrastructure handoff to production delivery. This role requires expertise in AWS services, system architecture, and cross-functional collaboration with Manufacturing, Operations, and Program Management teams to deliver AI/ML infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities
The Software Development Engineer (SDE II) on the EC2 UltraServer Delivery team is responsible for delivering production-ready GB200 and GB300 UltraServers to customers by orchestrating complex multi-asset provisioning workflows. Following are the core responsibilities

System Design & Architecture

* Design and architect solutions that are cross-functional to Manufacturing, Operations, and Program Management
* Work in environments where the technology strategy is defined but the solution design is not
* Build solutions that are stable, logical, testable, and efficient with the ability to independently make trade-off decisions
* Investigate and develop design concepts to frame solution sets at an application and product level

Software Development

* Build cloud-based solutions using AWS native services for scaling infrastructure frameworks
* Write high-quality, maintainable code with proper testing and code reviews
* Develop and maintain the Multi-Asset Provisioning Service workflows for GB200 and GB300 UltraServer hosts
* Implement automation for hardware testing, cable validation, and testing processes
* Create observable systems with appropriate metrics and alarming

Operational Excellence

* Execute and monitor UltraServer workflows for UltraServer provisioning
* Troubleshoot workflow failures and coordinate with downstream teams
* Focus on operational excellence by identifying problems and proposing solutions that improve manufacturing software

Hardware & Software Integration

* Work with hardware and software integrations specific to GPU clusters and AI/ML training systems
* Manage network partition configurations for multi-node GPU clusters
* Handle firmware validation and consistency checks across asset groups

Team Collaboration

* Collaborate with customers and stakeholders to convert business needs into technical designs
* Participate in code reviews and technical assessments


A day in the life
This is a hands-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.

About the team
The EC2 UltraServer Provisioning team is a high-performing engineering organization responsible for delivering NVIDIA-based ML infrastructure at scale. We manage end-to-end provisioning workflows for GB200 and GB300 UltraServers, from host ingestion through testing, repair, and recovery. Our team drives operational excellence through continuous improvement of build quality metrics, reduction of dwell times, and collaboration on fleet-wide unsellable reduction initiatives. We work closely with hardware engineering, data center operations, and EC2 service teams to ensure reliable, efficient delivery of critical ML compute capacity. This is a high-impact role leading a two-pizza team of talented engineers solving complex technical challenges in one of Amazon's fastest-growing infrastructure domains.

jobs.title: Kernel / Hypervisor Engineer - Firecracker, Firecracker
jobs.description:
Join us at AWS Lambda in building global scale compute platforms. We focus on serverless & container virtualization technologies, on trusted compute, and on server fleet tooling. We invent, build, and own building blocks that are the foundation of the cloud. This is an exciting opportunity for you to create new products and services of an innovative team that feels like a start-up!
We are looking for a new teammate who is enthusiastic, curious, empathic, motivated, reliable, with a good sense of ownership, and a drive to invent. In this role, you will work on Firecracker [1], an open source virtualization technology that is purpose-built for creating and managing secure, multi-tenant container and function-based services that provide serverless operational models. . Firecracker is deployed globally as part of AWS Lambda [2], Aurora D-SQL, and other AWS services. Firecracker is also integrated by 10+ teams beyond AWS as part of their platforms [3]. Firecracker has an ambitious multi-year roadmap of tackling impactful and interesting opportunities in the quickly expanding ephemeral compute space - come help us make history!

Your main goal will be to create long-term customer value. You will: work to understand our customers' needs and engineer new features to meet them; own and automate operations; contribute new ideas and methods to continuously improve quality and development efficiency; innovate in the area of ephemeral compute platforms; and be a maintainer of the Firecracker open source project. This position also involves on-call responsibilities, which is typically done once every 8 weeks. We strive to keep this down and ensure our systems are fault tolerant. Our team values work-life balance and we respect each others time.

At Amazon, we are dedicated to making new team members feel welcome and included. We are a team that strives to grow each other through task assignments, mentorship, and trainings. As an Amazonian, you’ll work with some of the most talented engineers in our industry. We believe in attracting, developing and retaining talent from diverse backgrounds. We value different perspectives and looking for team players who are working effectively with teams of diverse peers.

[1] https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker
[2] https://aws.amazon.com/lambda
[3] https://firecracker-microvm.github.io

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Marketing Cloud Assistant
jobs.description:
Application deadline: Nov 14, 2026

Build the AI-powered conversational agent that's transforming how advertisers interact with their data—replacing SQL queries and complex UIs with natural language that simply works. You'll work at the intersection of large language models, distributed systems, and petabyte-scale advertising data, shipping a high-visibility product at the forefront of generative AI in advertising.

We're looking for a Software Development Engineer II who is excited to solve hard, novel problems: natural language understanding, data accuracy at scale, agent evaluation, and translating complex analytical workflows into intuitive AI-driven experiences.

In this role, you will:

- Design and build core backend services powering an LLM-based conversational assistant for Amazon Marketing Cloud
- Own end-to-end delivery of features—from system design through production deployment and operational excellence
- Build scalable data pipelines and infrastructure that ingest and process petabyte-scale advertising data from multiple sources
- Shape the future of how advertisers generate insights, build audiences, and optimize campaigns through AI

This is a fast-paced, ownership-driven environment where you'll collaborate across science, product, and engineering to ship products that directly impact how millions of advertisers succeed on Amazon.

Who We're Looking For
We seek someone with a strong coding foundation and experience building distributed systems at scale—someone energized by ambiguity and fast-moving problem spaces. Ideal candidates bring curiosity about LLM-based applications and a track record of delivering customer-facing products end to end. Experience with advertising technology, analytics platforms, or AWS services is a plus.

Key job responsibilities
AI Assistant Platform
- Design, develop, and maintain backend services powering the AMC conversational assistant
- Build and optimize LLM orchestration pipelines including prompt engineering, tool use, and agent workflows
- Develop APIs and integrations with AMC's query engine, reporting services, and audience management systems
- Collaborate with applied scientists to integrate ML models and improve response quality
- Contribute to the evaluation framework—designing metrics, building ground truth datasets, and improving agent accuracy

Data Infrastructure
- Implement and maintain scalable data pipelines to ingest, process, and store petabyte-scale log-level advertising data from multiple sources (ad servers, exchanges, SSPs)
- Build ETL workflows that transform raw event-level data into queryable, analysis-ready formats following established architectural patterns
- Create and maintain APIs that enable analytics teams and data scientists to query log-level data efficiently
- Implement data quality checks, validation logic, and monitoring for data pipelines and services
- Optimize performance and cost efficiency of data processing jobs and queries

Engineering Excellence
- Own end-to-end delivery of features from design through production deployment
- Write clean, well-tested code and participate in code reviews to maintain high engineering standards
- Improve system reliability, latency, and scalability as the product scales to more advertisers
- Debug and resolve production issues, participating in on-call rotations as needed
- Document systems, processes, and runbooks to support operational excellence
- Collaborate with senior engineers to contribute to design discussions and architectural decisions

About the team
The Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC) Assistant team is building an AI-powered conversational agent that helps advertisers interact with AMC through natural language. We are developing LLM-based experiences that simplify complex analytical workflows—enabling advertisers to generate insights, build audiences, and optimize campaigns without writing SQL or navigating complex UIs. Our work sits at the intersection of generative AI, advertising technology, and large-scale data systems.
