Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.



Key job responsibilities
Design, implement, and enhance the switch-management software — from translating routes received from a centralized SDN controller into forwarding-table entries, to building MAC-learning and loop-prevention logic for a redundant switch topology — that enables deterministic, low-latency packet forwarding across the constellation

Design and optimize the networking layers of flight software for optical inter-satellite link systems, spanning network device drivers and protocol implementations on embedded Linux

Collaborate with cross-functional teams — including hardware, optics, systems, communications, and operations engineers — to integrate, test, and deploy high-speed optical communication systems and the networking stack that underpins space-based connectivity

Build and extend operational tooling for network diagnostics and observability — including routing-table inspection, packet capture and analysis, structured logging, and metrics emission — that enables rapid fault isolation and performance trending across the satellite mesh












A day in the life
As a Software Engineer on the Optical Inter-Satellite Link team, you won't just write code — you'll see it fly. Your software will control and monitor high-speed laser communications between satellites moving at orbital velocities, and you'll be there for every stage of the journey: from early design and ground-based verification to watching your code commission an optical link for the first time in orbit. On the networking side, you'll design and debug the switching fabric that routes traffic across the constellation — ensuring packets traverse inter-satellite links with minimal latency and maximum reliability.






About the team
You will join a multi-disciplinary team of exceptional engineers whose work spans an unusually broad scope: embedded flight software running on satellites in orbit, cloud-based systems powering mission and network operations, automation frameworks that keep a growing constellation healthy, and AI-driven capabilities that make our optical links smarter with every orbit. We collaborate closely with optical, electrical, firmware, opto-mechanical, and operations teams — and with partner organizations including Mission Operations and Optical Network Operations — to deliver one of the most advanced optical communication systems ever built.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer II, On Road Execution

- Design and operate Tier-1 services at up to 99.95% uptime, absorbing 2-3X traffic during peak

- Drive a live architecture migration and re-architect our enrichment platform to an event-driven model

- Work in a GenAI-forward team where AI tooling is part of how every engineer builds

Key job responsibilities
As a Backend SDE on ORE, you'll design, build, test, and operate mission-critical Tier-1 distributed services at scale, owning your work end to end — from design through launch and into production on-call. You will:

- Develop FIPS (FlexItineraryProviderService), the aggregator between backend systems and the Rabbit app — gathering sequence (IM), assignment (PTRAS), and TR metadata (PTRS), enriching in parallel, and translating into Rabbit models.
- Build on Itinerary Manager (IM), our materialized-view system of record, storing stops and tasks in DynamoDB/S3 and publishing change notifications via SNS.
- Evolve PTRAS, our transport-request assignment authority and Common Dispatcher Interface.
- Drive the Task-Based Architecture (TBAR) migration toward a contract/task model enabling multi-action deliveries.
- Re-architect our enrichment platform from synchronous pull to event-driven push without sacrificing consistency.
- Help stand up a new Tier-1 service at 99.95% from day one.
- Review designs and code from Partner teams building into our platform.

A day in the life
You'll spend your day designing and building backend services, writing and reviewing code, and shepherding changes through launch and into production. You'll collaborate with product managers, upstream route-planning teams, and the Rabbit app team, and review designs and CRs from Speed program teams building into our platform. As an owner of Tier-1 services, you'll take part in on-call — and when high-severity events strike, you'll be central to diagnosing root causes and mitigating impact on the end-to-end driver experience. Expect deep distributed-systems problems, real autonomy, and impact measured in packages delivered.

About the team
The On-Road Execution (ORE) team, part of the TransporterX org within Amazon's Last Mile Technology, owns the backend that manages the execution state of every driver's itinerary — the interface between route planning, station operations, and the Rabbit driver app. Our systems support delivery across a 10+ billion shipment base spanning 21 countries, powering same-day and ultra-fast programs like Quick Commerce and Premium SSD. We're a GenAI-forward team where AI tooling is part of how every engineer works, and we've turned operational excellence into a discipline — resilience-scenario mapping, fast rollback tooling, and load-shedding SOPs that carry us through record peaks. We're modernizing our architecture toward cleaner boundaries while running Tier-1 services at up to 99.95% uptime.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Vulnerability Management
jobs.description:

Within the organization, our team owns host operating system vulnerability management, and our job is to mitigate the highest security risks at machine speed and at the lowest cost to AWS. We find the hardest security problems in our fleet, build prototypes, iterate fast, and reduce the attack surface so vulnerabilities never reach production hosts. Working with some of the largest services at AWS like EC2, S3, RDS, SageMaker, and Amazon Linux means diving deep into operating systems, fleet automation, and security data at AWS scale.

The successful candidate is one who turns a hard security problem into a service that solves it fleet wide. You will build the systems that determine why vulnerabilities persist across millions of hosts, predict which ones will become critical before they do, and drive remediation without a human in the loop, moving mean time to remediate down and cutting the engineering hours AWS spends on patching. You will work directly with AWS service teams and partner security teams, prototype fast, and take what works from prototype to production. We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations: Seattle, WA

Key job responsibilities
Build the systems that determine why vulnerabilities persist across the AWS host fleet and drive them to remediation automatically.

Build detection that identifies where patching automation is not reaching hosts, and route what it finds to the owning team.

Prototype fast against fleet-scale security data, then take what works to production and own it there, including on-call.

Partner with AWS service teams and security platform teams to reduce the attack surface across the fleet.

A day in the life

You will prototype an idea, prove it against real fleet data, and take the ones that work into production. You will work directly with AWS service teams to turn what you find into remediation they can act on immediately. The team is security engineers with deep fleet expertise, a technical program manager, and a support engineer, and the engineering team is growing.

About the team

We find the hardest problems keeping vulnerabilities alive in the fleet, build the services that eliminate them, and work directly with the AWS service teams who run that fleet. You will build security services that protect AWS from real adversaries, at a scale where the solution has to be automatic. The engineering team is growing and the scope grows with it.

jobs.title: Sr. ECAD Systems Engineer, Configuration Management
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

We are seeking a software-fluent ECAD Interdisciplinary Systems Engineer to join the Engineering Practice & Configuration Management team. This role mirrors the mechanical domain's custom tooling function-you will build the integration tooling and automation that connects EE design systems (Xpedition, EDM, Teamcenter) into a seamless, reliable configuration management backbone.

You will build the connective tissue between EE's core design systems—Xpedition, EDM, and Teamcenter—creating intelligent automation for IDX exchanges, component synchronization, and BOM reconciliation that eliminates manual handoffs and scales with the program. This will result into a world-class tooling velocity and cross-system reliability for the EE domain.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
• Custom Integration Tooling: Design, build, and maintain automation that synchronizes data across Xpedition, EDM, and Teamcenter-keeping the 6000+ part component library dimensionally consistent and properly linked across all systems
• BOM Reconciliation Automation: Build tooling that guarantees Teamcenter BOM, Xpedition BOM, and supply-chain BOMs match at design release; enable where-used analysis; flag missing or dropped components; block PCBA release when parts are out of sync or unreleased
• IDX Exchange Improvement: Automate and harden the ECAD-MCAD collaboration workflow (IDX process); implement the validated scheme file as default configuration; build guardrails that prevent protocol deviations that destroy design history
• Build-to-Design Loop Closure: Pull as-built BOM data from supply-chain systems and contract manufacturer red-lines back into engineering tools, enabling true end-to-end data accuracy
• Component Dimensional Integrity Tooling: Build automated verification that detects and prevents dimensional mismatches of component definition between EDM and Teamcenter to enable identification PCBA-to-enclosure fitment failures in CAD and before fabrication
• Release Workflow Automation: Develop release gates and automated checks that enforce component maturity requirements, BOM consistency, and data completeness before PCBA release approval
• Tooling Backlog Ownership: Maintain and prioritize the EE tooling backlog (mirroring mechanical's 47+ item backlog); partner with the EE Configuration Manager to identify highest-impact automation opportunities
• Cross-Domain Integration: Ensure EE tooling integrates cleanly with existing in-house designed mechanical tooling infrastructure for unified cross-domain workflows
• Developer Documentation: Maintain technical documentation for all custom tooling, APIs, and integrations to ensure sustainability and team knowledge transfer

A day in the life
You will be responsible to work across multiple engineering functions to understand the daily pain points of a responsible engineering and translating those into the custom ECAD tools for EE domain.

About the team
The Configuration Management team develops and governs the engineering systems, standards, and processes that ensure spacecraft design data remains accurate, traceable, and controlled throughout the product lifecycle. While the organization originated as a traditional design support function, it has evolved into the engineering authority for product data management and engineering configuration.

The team defines how engineering information flows throughout the digital engineering environment, including Product Lifecycle Management workflows, mechanical and electrical design tool integration, engineering data management, and the interaction between Teamcenter, Siemens NX, Mentor, and other engineering platforms. They also develop tooling and automation that improves engineering productivity while maintaining data integrity across these systems.

In addition to managing engineering data, the organization serves as the company's subject matter experts in Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing. They develop engineering standards, mentor design engineers, and promote best practices that improve drawing quality, manufacturability, and technical consistency across the organization.

The team also defines and continuously improves the organization's configuration and change management processes for hardware, requirements, and engineering documentation. They work closely with software organizations to strengthen integrated hardware and software configuration control while ensuring traceability throughout the development lifecycle. Today the organization facilitates Engineering Change Committee and Configuration Control Board activities while actively developing increasingly automated workflows in partnership with the Engineering Information Systems team. These efforts continue moving the organization toward a more efficient, data driven approach to engineering governance.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer, Amazon Leo Satellite Broadband Terminals
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.

What you'll work on:
• Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
• Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
• Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
• RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
• System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

Key job responsibilities
What we look for:
• Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware.
• Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it.
• Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system.

Our stack:
Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life
As part of our BSP software engineering team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Kuiper products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues.

We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS OpenSearch Service
jobs.description:
Imagine running search and analytics at any scale without thinking about clusters, capacity, or version upgrades. Where your queries return in milliseconds whether you're indexing a thousand documents or a hundred billion. Where the platform scales, heals, and secures itself so your team can focus on the questions, not the infrastructure.

That's what we build.

Amazon OpenSearch Service is the fully managed and Serverless AWS service that lets customers deploy, operate, and scale OpenSearch for log analytics, full-text search, application monitoring, observability, and AI-powered retrieval. We serve hundreds of thousands of customers running mission-critical workloads across every AWS region, and we are part of the AWS Database and Analytics organization.

Come join the OpenSearch Control Plane team. We are responsible for a service that:

- Reliably manages a large fleet of cloud-native OpenSearch clusters and collections, freeing customers from sizing, scaling, and patching decisions
- Guarantees high availability and durability for mission-critical search and observability workloads at the scale of the most demanding internet businesses
- Orchestrates and automates the complete lifecycle of an OpenSearch cluster or collection — from creation through scale-up, scale-out, upgrade, replication, and fail-over

The OpenSearch control plane is not just any distributed system. It orchestrates a fleet of clusters across every AWS region, detects and recovers from node failures in seconds, and serves workloads that span petabytes of customer data. Most recently, we launched **OpenSearch Serverless NextGen** — delivering ultra-fast collection provisioning and true scale-to-zero capacity, so customers pay only for what they use and get a working environment in seconds rather than minutes. We are not done; this is one of many investments raising the bar for what customers can expect from a managed search service.

OpenSearch itself is a community-driven, Apache 2.0–licensed open-source search and analytics suite built on Apache Lucene. Since launching in July 2021, the project has delivered multiple major and minor releases advancing core search, vector search, and analytics. Our next phase focuses on transforming OpenSearch into an intelligent retrieval engine — one that meets the evolving needs of customers running search, analytics, and AI-powered workloads across structured, unstructured, and multi-modal data.

We work in Java, Rust, Python, and Go. We contribute upstream to OpenSearch and Apache Lucene. We are customer-obsessed, operate with the entrepreneurial pace of a startup inside one of the world's largest cloud providers, and value strong intuition backed by metrics.

**Operations is core engineering on this team, not overhead.** Engineers operate what they build, and we treat customer-impacting incidents with the same engineering rigor we apply to feature work. Reliability and Static Stability is a forcing function for design, not a phase after launch.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and operate components of a large-scale distributed control plane — reason about failure modes, multi-tenant isolation, and blast-radius before writing code
- Look for opportunities to simplify — consolidate duplicate abstractions, remove dead code, reduce configuration sprawl, and challenge complexity that doesn't earn its keep
- Treat operations as core engineering — own the systems you build end-to-end, participate fully in incident response and RCAs, and drive operational improvements that reduce cost and maintenance burden
- Solve real problems in cluster orchestration, capacity provisioning, lifecycle workflows, multi-tenant infrastructure, query routing, and operational tooling
- Use AI coding assistants and GenAI tools effectively across the software development lifecycle — from design and prototyping through coding, testing, code review, debugging, and operations — applying engineering judgment to validate AI-generated output against Amazon's correctness, security, and operational bar
- Write robust, efficient, and maintainable code in Java, Rust, Python, or Go
- Partner with senior engineers to translate ambiguous requirements into concrete deliverables; prototype, test, and validate
- Continually challenge what exists and explore what should change to better serve customers

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, Profit Intelligence
jobs.description:
Are you interested in building intelligence systems from the ground up?

Are you interested in working with Applied Scientists, Big Data Engineers and Software Development Engineers to build large-scale data intelligence systems?

Are you interested to work in a team that positively impacts different key pillars of Amazon like Pricing, Promotions, Advertising, Auto inventory purchasing, Auto inventory removal, Inventory placement?

Are you interested in working for a team that builds cool systems yet has great work-life balance?

Profit intelligence systems measures, predicts true profit(/loss) for each item as a result of a specific shipment to an Amazon customer.

Prot Intelligence is all about providing intelligent ways for Amazon to understand profitability across retail business. What are the hidden factors driving the growth or profitability across millions of shipments each day?

Profit Intelligence provides these answers.

We compute the profitability of each and every shipment that gets shipped out of Amazon. Guess what, we predict the profitability of future possible shipments too. We are a team of agile, can-do engineers, who believe that not only are moon shots possible but that they can be done before lunch. All it takes is finding new ideas that challenge our preconceived notions of how things should be done. Process and procedure matter less than ideas and the practical work of getting stuff done. This is a place for exploring the new and taking risks.

We push the envelope in using cloud services in AWS as well as the latest in distributed systems, forecasting algorithms, and data mining.

We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to design and build AI-powered data platforms that transform large-scale business data into actionable insights. You will work at the intersection of machine learning, distributed systems, and data engineering — owning end-to-end development of tools that help business leaders make faster, better decisions.
This is a high-impact role on a team where the software you ship directly shapes financial and operational strategy across Amazon.

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities

Architect and build scalable platforms that ingest, process, and serve insights from petabyte-scale datasets
Integrate large language models and generative AI capabilities into internal analytics tools — enabling natural language querying, anomaly explanation, and automated reporting
Design ML pipelines for anomaly detection, forecasting, and trend analysis over structured and semi-structured business data
Partner with scientists, analysts, and PMs to translate ambiguous business problems into well-scoped technical solutions
Drive engineering excellence: define coding standards, lead design reviews, and set the bar for operational health (monitoring, oncall, runbooks)
Mentor junior engineers; raise the technical capability of the team through clear documentation and code review
Own your services in production — you build it, you run it
Build and operate our foundational data infrastructure comprising of the entire spectrum of AWS Services - Storage (Redshift Data Shares, s3 data lakes), Orchestration (Step Functions, Glue and Internal Java Based Orchestration Tools), Processing (Spark & Flink - KDA), Streaming services (AWS Kinesis) and real-time large scale event aggregation stores.
Making it fully configurable and self-service for non-engineers.
Build and evolve tools that empower Amazonians to access data and build reliable, scalable and configurable way to generate Unit Economics for all Amazon Businesses. This includes UIs and frameworks for configuring rules, simulating their application, approval workows for rule changes, APIs and caching layers for high-throughput serving of Unit Economics Historicals and Predictions.
Build systems that secure and govern our data end to end: control access across multiple storage and access layers (like inhouse Reporting Applications and BI tools), track data quality, catalogue datasets and their lineage, detect duplication, audit usage and ensure correct data semantics.
You will be responsible for designing and building platforms for crunching 100s of TB of in-coming data from dozens of sources and financial events around the company.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, 1P Audio Video Measurement
jobs.description:
We build first-party measurement solutions that help advertisers understand the performance and impact of their audio and video campaigns across Amazon's advertising platforms—including Online Video Ads, Streaming TV, Live Sports, Sponsored Brands Video, Sponsored Display Video, and Audio Ads, which means our solutions must work at a massive scale. jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, AWS Networking Reasoning Team
jobs.description:
The AWS network changes constantly, and every change carries risk. A single bad configuration can pull capacity offline or disrupt customer traffic. Validating that a change is safe at AWS scale is hard: a single change interacts with thousands of variables across a global network, and the complexity grows faster than the size does. That challenge is now increasing in a new way. Network teams are building their own software services that manage network behavior directly, and they need to propose, test, and release a change in minutes opposed to weeks. Our team builds the platforms that let them do that without giving up reliability.

We build the software that tells a network builder whether a proposed change is safe before it reaches production. That means formal verification of device configurations, large-scale network simulation and emulation, and automated testing that models how the network will behave under a change. We turn those capabilities into self-service guardrails that any network team can adopt and trust, so they own their safety decisions and still move fast. The hard part is keeping the checks correct and general as the network evolves, and fast enough that builders rely on them instead of routing around them.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who can design systems with demanding functional and non-functional requirements, working alongside network engineers and applied scientists to deliver value continuously. You will be a hands-on technical lead across the full development cycle: partnering with internal customers to understand their problems, generating technical designs, and carrying projects from implementation through validation and operations.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, AWS Transfer Family
jobs.description:
AWS Transfer Family (launched at re:Invent 2018) is looking for talented engineers with a passion for solving challenging problems to join the team and help us take the service to the next level. AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service supporting file transfers over different file transfer protocols for AWS Storage Services like Amazon S3. AWS Transfer Family helps customers seamlessly migrate file transfer workflows to AWS, freeing customers from managing, operating and securing their own file transfer solution. Customers can easily create file transfer endpoints that allow their business partners to easily send files directly to AWS Storage such as AWS S3. We are looking for a team member to understand the B2B file transfer and transactional needs of enterprises across key verticals and geographies as they migrate to the cloud and what new file transfer products and features we should build to accelerate such migrations and unlock value from AWS integrations.

What makes this role exciting is that every day brings new challenges as customer workloads grow and technology evolves. Much of your time will be hands-on with our systems.

You might be:
* Designing and writing code to delight our customers to deliver an impactful feature, adding optimization functions to scale the performance and so on.
* Diving into data to make design decisions or measure effectiveness of changes you make.
* Debugging complex distributed systems issues that require careful analysis and creative problem-solving.
* Review proposals and code from peers from the team as well as partner teams.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Our senior engineers truly enjoy mentoring more junior engineers and engineers from non-traditional backgrounds through one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews.

We care about your career growth. We try to assign projects and tasks based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded engineer and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Leo AI Foundations
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Role
This role is for a Software Engineer who will design, implement, and operate globally distributed systems that enable Leo to achieve low single-digit-second query responses within a near real-time analytics layer or lakehouse, and to support agentic AI capabilities on top. You’ll build these systems using the latest AWS technologies and best-in-industry software engineering practices.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Architect and implement a scalable, cost-optimized S3-based Data Lakehouse that unifies structured and unstructured data from disparate sources.
- Architect and implement a scalable, cost-performance-optimized OLAP-based analytics layer
- Establish metadata management with automated data classification and lineage tracking.
- Design and enforce standardized data ingestion patterns with built-in quality controls and validation gates.
- Architect a centralized metrics repository that becomes the source of truth for all Leo metrics.
- Implement robust data quality frameworks with staging-first policies and automated validation pipelines.
- Design extensible metrics schemas that support complex analytical queries while optimizing for AI retrieval patterns.
- Develop intelligent orchestration for metrics generation workflows with comprehensive audit trails.
- Lead the design of semantic data models that balance analytical performance with AI retrieval requirements.
- Implement cross-domain federated query capabilities with sophisticated query optimization techniques.
- Architect a globally distributed vector database infrastructure capable of managing billions of embeddings with consistent sub-100ms retrieval times.
- Design and implement hybrid search strategies combining dense vectors with sparse representations for optimal semantic retrieval.
- Establish automated compliance validation frameworks ensuring data handling meets Amazon's security standards.

A day in the life
This role is for a Software Development Engineer who will build new cloud services and APIs that facilitate and orchestrate the Leo AI Foundations—enabling intelligent software operation across Leo devices such as satellites, ground gateways, and customer terminals. You will design and deliver low-latency, highly scalable architectures that are critical to providing high-quality internet service and AI capabilities to customers.

About the team
Amazon Leo AI Foundations builds the intelligent cloud backbone that powers AI-driven decision making across Amazon’s Leo constellation — from satellites and ground gateways to customer terminals. Our team designs and operates large-scale data and compute systems that enable training, inference, and agentic intelligence for optimizing network performance, routing, and user experience in real time. We combine expertise in distributed systems, data lakehouse architectures, and applied machine learning to deliver scalable, low-latency AI capabilities that integrate seamlessly with Leo's software-defined space and ground systems. We move fast, innovate boldly, and work across boundaries to make global connectivity smarter and more efficient.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer II, Ring Quick Action Service
jobs.description:
At Amazon, we are continuously striving to be Earth’s most customer-centric company. Our Ring Quick Action Service (QAS) team is at the heart of this goal, ensuring that we can harness the power of data to innovate and improve the experience for millions of customers around the world. We are looking for an experienced Software Development Engineer to build and scale our QAS systems.

Ring is expanding and this role will be key in the development of solutions for collecting, storing, and analyzing vast amounts of data. This role will both inherit existing and build new services to enhance observability across Ring devices, mobile apps, and cloud services.

If you are passionate about connecting millions of devices through data, deriving meaning from this data, have a proven engineering record, and want to make an enormous impact, this might be the role for you!


Key job responsibilities
- Own the overall systems development technical life cycle for team services.
- Guide the evolution of the team to offer real time search and analysis across RBKS organizations
- Develop tools to scale and manage large data clusters, automate onboarding of data, and develop self-service interfaces for the data management lifecycle.
- Maintain and support new integrations for our LogSynth MCP solution, RAG knowledge base, and REST-based API interfaces.
- Liaison to service teams to understand existing data sets and evaluate emerging technologies in the Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence areas.
- Understand existing data streams and develop metrics from them to measure the customer experience, implement predictive modeling for proactive monitoring of KPI’s.
- Evaluate the current ecosystem for log analytic plugins for customer value and write custom plugins to add insight into our service teams and customer metrics.
- Define a strategy for software unit, functional and performance testing; lead code review sessions with team.
- Implement optimal security practices while scaling existing and new data services.
- Contribute to operational excellence practices within the team and perform one week of on-call rotation a maximum of every four weeks.
- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to align solutions with business needs.
- Ensure best practices and architectural guidelines are followed, with a strong focus on cloud-optimized solutions.

A day in the life
- Build automation and self-service solutions.
- Participate in Operation Excellence reviews to spot negative trends before they become production issues.
- Contribute to code bases and peer review for infrastructure as well as supporting services.
- Help key stakeholders in a variety of security and application groups across Ring with data ingestion and analytic projects.

About the team
You will be joining a veteran team with several members who have 4+ years experience at Ring and Amazon. Ring doorbells and security products are part of neighborhoods across the country, so you can take pride in supporting a tangible product that helps our Neighbors be safe.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Customer Terminals Applications & Networking Team
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks — from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo Customer Terminal Application and Networking Team builds the on-device software that runs on the customer's antenna and turns it into a fast, reliable, self-diagnosing internet gateway. As a Software Development Engineer II on this team, you will design and build software that operates on customer terminals deployed in the field at large scale — where there is no physical access and connectivity can be intermittent. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, networking, and cloud teams to take features from design through testing and launch.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
Improve the speed and reliability of the customer's internet connection on the terminal.
- Build software that gives customers and support teams the tools to detect and resolve issues on their own, reducing the need for on-site visits.
- Deliver device health and diagnostics data from the fleet reliably and efficiently, so engineering has visibility into how terminals are performing in the field.
- Own features end to end — design, implementation, testing, code review, deployment, and validation on live hardware — writing high-quality, maintainable code.
- Debug complex issues that span hardware, software, and the cloud, and raise the operational bar for software running on a rapidly growing production fleet.
- Collaborate with hardware, firmware, networking, and cloud teams to deliver features that meet quality and performance bars for launch.

About the team
We build the software that lives on the customer's terminal — powering its connectivity, performance, and self-service diagnostics across a rapidly growing global fleet.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer , Amazon Leo Network Services
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
* You will develop code, build CI/CD pipelines, test automation, and dashboards for monitoring health of systems and data pipelines.
* You will work with multiple cross functional teams to gather requirements, design, develop, deploy, and operate the infrastructure you build
* You will develop and mentor junior and new team members.
* You will engineer and build a cloud service that is reliable and available to provide connectivity for our customers
* You will work on features that enhance the quality of service and security for our customers.
* You will collaborate and work on initiatives across multiple teams to build networking functions on AWS cloud infrastructure and set best practices for software development processes.

A day in the life
You'll design and operate software that manages the lifecycle of every customer terminal antenna in Kuiper's LEO constellation — from provisioning and configuration through firmware updates and fleet operations at global scale.

On any given day you might build APIs orchestrating over-the-air updates across thousands of terminals, solve distributed systems challenges like certificate revocation and location-aware routing, or drive operational excellence for services supporting real customer traffic 24/7. You'll collaborate closely with embedded software, network operations, security, and platform teams to keep every terminal secure, connected, and current.

About the team
The CT Overlay team builds the services that bring Kuiper's customer terminal antennas to life. We own device identity, configuration management, firmware delivery, fleet orchestration, and location services — the software layer that sits manages the fleet of physical hardware and their management on the network. Our systems operate at constellation scale, managing tens of thousands of terminals across multiple regions with strict security and availability requirements. We move fast, ship often, and own what we build end-to-end — from design through production operations. If you like solving real distributed systems problems with immediate customer impact, this is the team.

jobs.title: Software Engineer- AI/ML, Amazon Neuron Training
jobs.description:
The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds AWS Neuron, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on AWS Trainium, Amazon's custom machine learning accelerator. Neuron includes an ML compiler, runtime, collectives library, and application framework that integrate with PyTorch and JAX, so customers can train frontier-scale models on Trainium without rewriting their stack.

The Distributed Training team is at the forefront of training a wide range of models on AWS's custom ML accelerators, supporting novel architectures while maximizing their training performance. Working across the stack from PyTorch and JAX down to the hardware and software boundary, our engineers build the infrastructure that large-scale training depends on, develop new parallelism and numerics techniques, and tune high-performance kernels for the operations that dominate a training step, so every compute unit is doing useful work on our customers' most demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the limits of training efficiency at scale.

As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers, from frameworks and kernels through to the compiler, runtime, and collectives teams. This is hardware and software co-design in practice. A single throughput gap rarely sits in one layer, so tracing it means following the problem across the stack, deciding where the fix belongs, and working with the team that owns that layer to land it. We not only optimize current performance but also contribute to future architecture designs, since the gaps we characterize today become requirements for the next generation of Trainium. We work closely with customers to enable their models and ensure they train efficiently. This role offers a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed systems, where you will help shape the direction of AI acceleration technology.



Key job responsibilities
Your role will help lead the effort to optimize distributed training performance on Trainium, with a primary focus on training throughput across the Neuron software stack. You will work across PyTorch and Neuron solftware stack with amazing Neuron compiler and runtime teams to enable and tune large-scale training workloads on the latest Trainium instances You will own the parallelism strategies these models depend on, spanning data, tensor, pipeline, expert, and context parallelism, and apply reduced-precision formats where they measurably pay off. You will profile end to end to determine whether a workload is bound by compute, memory, collectives, or host overhead, then drive the fix to the layer that owns it, working with compiler, runtime, and collectives engineers to land it. You will translate the performance gaps you characterize into requirements that influence frameworks, and contribute upstream to the open source frameworks our customers train on.

We have innovative benefit offerings, and host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Autopilot
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.


Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Work with our peer teams and customers to design suitable software systems to fulfill the mission needs.
- Develop cloud native software systems in Java and Python.
- Utilize AWS and other Amazon technologies to build highly-available software services.
- Design and develop performant software systems that meet the mission criteria and requirements.
- Help on-board and mentor new team members.
- Lead technical roadmap definition efforts and decide which features and performance improvements to build.

A day in the life
As a Software Development Engineer, you will play a crucial role in the development of services to support the automation of the Leo mission. You will work with a dynamic group of passionate engineers and collaborators across peer teams to identify automation needs, design novel solutions that meet customer requirements, and write software to automate key behaviors for our constellation's space and ground assets. You will be building low-latency, highly-scalable architecture to generate and execute our mission plans safely and effectively.

About the team
The Autopilot team builds software which supports the automated planning and execution of satellite activities, empowering humans to automate key tasks and take themselves out of the loop as we scale the Leo constellation. We own services that model spacecraft behaviors, predict future vehicle state, capture operational constraints on our system, and generate mission schedules that serve our customers while preserving vehicle health and safety.

AFT builds and operates software, hardware, and processes that run the global network of fulfillment centers that move many billions of units of inventory, employ tens of thousands of people, and ensure that customers get what they want when we promised we would get it to them. We do this by building automated solutions to handle things that technology does well, while relying on people to handle things that humans do well.

Our Flow systems automate the flow and labor management decisions within the fulfillment facilities. From the moment inventory is scheduled to arrive into the fulfillment center it is processed and stowed to ensure its readiness to fulfill customer orders. Once the order is placed the inventory is picked and the customer shipment flows through various manual and robotic processes up until customer package leaves the fulfillment facility on its way to the customer. Our systems ensure fast and optimal flow within the building by putting just the right resources at the right locations while automatically surfacing and resolving any unforeseen risks to ensure Amazon Associate safety and experience and help Amazon to constantly keep its promise to the customers while optimizing and expanding its business operations.

We are looking for a talented SDE to build best-in-class user experiences for managing and communicating one of the most critical elements of fulfillment operations - staffing assignments. jobs.title: Systems Development Engineer II, AWS WorkSpaces, Agentic Workspaces
jobs.description:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work, not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workspaces will host AI agents alongside humans — agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users, governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft, Citrix, and Omnissa, and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era, not retrofitted for it.

Agentic Workspaces' On-Instance Software (OIS) is the layer that makes this possible from the inside of every WorkSpace: the operating-system provisioning logic, on-instance agents, telemetry, and update mechanisms across Windows and Linux. Our vision is for that software to be invisible — operating systems that launch within weeks of upstream general availability, agents that update themselves safely without disrupting access, provisioning that is self-diagnosable, and fleet management that works through the same AWS tools customers already use — delivered from commercial regions to classified partitions with automation as the default, so quality and breadth improve release over release.

Knowledge of Linux operating systems, Linux package management, and native Linux desktop application development is desired.

You want to solve challenging problems in operating systems, identity, AI, and desktop platform engineering at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily.

We are looking for cross platform systems development engineers who are passionate about building, maintaining, and automating the systems that underpin the robust WorkSpaces-fleet system. On any given day we use Python, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudFormation, PowerShell, as well as other public AWS services and a host of Amazon-internal tools. We don't expect you to be an expert in or necessarily even be familiar with all of the technologies listed above, but we do expect you to be excited to learn about them!

In this role you'll help WorkSpaces-Fleet expand into new regions, remove development friction through automation, and collaborate with a team of Systems Developers to help shape the future for the next generation of services to help customers reduce the mean-time-to manage their WorkSpaces. You'll apply your creative and critical problem solving skills to develop and run multi-tenant services at massive scale.

You are customer-obsessed, technically deep, and energized by solving hard problems. You think big about what the workspace of the future looks like — a unified agent shipping to two platforms from one code base, an identity model that treats humans and agents as first-class citizens, and autonomous troubleshooting that resolves issues before users notice — and then you build the systems to get there.

Key job responsibilities
In this role you'll help WorkSpaces-Fleet expand into new regions, remove development friction through automation, and collaborate with a team of Systems Developers to help shape the future for the next generation of services to help customers reduce the mean-time-to manage their WorkSpaces. You'll apply your creative and critical problem solving skills to develop and run multi-tenant services at massive scale.


About the team
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Amazon Leo Optical Inter-Satellite Link
jobs.description:
Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon LEO will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

Innovation is part of our DNA! Our goal is to be Earth’s most customer centric company, and we are just getting started. We need people who want to join this ambitious program that continues to push the state of the art in distributed systems and software design. Come work at Amazon!

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.




Key job responsibilities
Design, develop, and optimize highly reliable flight software for optical inter-satellite link systems, spanning low-level device drivers and real-time control loops to high-level autonomous behaviors, fault management, and AI/ML-driven decision-making that target embedded linux and RTOS (Real Time Operating System)

Architect and implement fault-tolerant, redundant software systems that keep optical links alive across a constellation of satellites, including health monitoring and autonomous recovery without ground intervention

Build and maintain robust test, validation, and simulation infrastructure, from hardware-in-the-loop testbeds and software-in-the-loop virtualizations to automated regression suites

Own the full lifecycle of embedded software delivery - from requirements decomposition and architecture design through implementation, code review, integration, deployment, and long-term maintenance of software running on satellites in orbit

Collaborate deeply with cross-functional teams spanning hardware, optics, systems, communications, and operations engineers to design, integrate, test, and deploy high-speed optical communication systems that push the boundaries of space-based networking

Drive continuous improvement of deployment and over-the-air (OTA) update processes, ensuring new capabilities and fixes can be safely and reliably delivered to hundreds of satellites on orbit with minimal operational risk

Partner with software and hardware teams to lead board bring-up and integration efforts, including developing and debugging low-level BSP (Board Support Package) components, validating peripheral connectivity (Ethernet, PCIe, SPI, I2C, flash devices), and ensuring seamless hardware-software integration from prototype through production





A day in the life
As a Software Engineer on the Optical Inter-Satellite Link team, you won't just write code - you'll see it fly. Your software will control and monitor high-speed laser communications between satellites moving at orbital velocities, and you'll be there for every stage of the journey: from early design and on-the-ground verifications to watching your code commission an optical link for the first time in orbit.

About the team
You will join a multi-disciplinary team of top-notch engineers whose work spans an unusually wide aperture: embedded flight software running on satellites in orbit, cloud-based systems powering mission and network operations, automation frameworks that keep a growing constellation healthy, and AI-driven capabilities that make our optical links smarter with every orbit. We collaborate closely with optical, electrical, firmware, opto-mechanical, and operations teams — and with partner organizations including Mission Operations and Optical Network Operations — to deliver one of the most advanced optical communication systems ever built.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, STRADA
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Service Transformation and Deployment Automation team aims to remove all manual touchpoints from service operations within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Networking, one of the world’s largest and most complex networks. Software Development Engineers are instrumental in discovering innovative ways to automate and scale services. They drive stability, consistency, and sustainability of the network while never losing sight of the high security bar our customer’s demand. We own a container compute platform in the border network, network device access and locality software, and a business intelligence platform for providing insights into service maturity. This position is located in Minneapolis, USA and working in the heart of AWS global network.

Millions of customers rely on Amazon’s network for using our retail websites, accessing content on their Kindles, and building applications and businesses on top of the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud. Our goal is to become The Infrastructure Platform for the world – achieving this goal requires automated and massively scalable software services. Success depends on our world-class network infrastructure, and our network depends on our automation.

This position involves on-call responsibilities, typically for one week every two months. We don’t like getting paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we work to ensure that our systems are fault tolerant. When we do get paged, we work together to resolve the root cause so that we don’t get paged for the same issue twice.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Our senior engineers truly enjoy mentoring more junior engineers and engineers from non-traditional backgrounds through one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth. We try to assign projects and tasks based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded engineer and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.


Key job responsibilities
You will be responsible for the design, implementation and quality of services you deliver. Your experience working in software development or in an enterprise environment will help us implement automated solutions across a variety of applications and systems.
You’ll also:
• Design, implement, test, deploy and maintain innovative solutions to transform service performance, durability, cost, and security.
• Write high quality distributed system software.
• Work in an agile, startup-like development environment, where you are always working on the most important stuff.
• Work closely with our Network/Systems/Software Engineering teams to ensure fast and smooth roll-out of new designs and products, as well as assist with deployment and sustaining of networking software tools.
• Use data to measure success and take responsibility for the quality of your service and, regardless of their source, strive to prevent faults from impacting your customers.
• Use your strong problem-solving skills, ability to understand and scope solutions, work across teams to drive solutions.
• Contribute to documentation of process and procedures.
• Learn from others and help grow those in your team to achieve their best.
• Take ownership, consider tradeoffs and lean on your expertise to ensure the job gets done.
• Participate in an on-call rotation with your team.

A day in the life
Engineers in the Backbone Enterprise and Regional Engineering (BERE) organization have a wide range
of responsibilities; we work with internal partners to develop and implement the next-generation platforms along with the tooling ecosystems to support these platforms driving efficiency and scalability through the automation of builds, configuration deployment, and the scaling of capacity. As our network is one of the largest in the world, there is no blueprint allowing our engineers to develop solutions to complex challenges that we face daily. We encourage durable solutions that
look around corners while taking into consideration our customer needs from a cost, performance, and
reliability perspective. Our team develops tooling that provides the required visibility and control of
traffic across the network, while prioritizing the automatic mitigation of events to minimize the impact
to our customers during events.
In this role you:
• Work in a 24x7 team on-call rotation, with ability to drive into workplace for critical events/needs.
• Manage customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure.
• Sit at the computer during scheduled work hours with appropriate breaks while maintaining a high level of alertness and attention to detail.
• Travel to data center/network sites and Amazon/customer offices as needed.

About the team
Within AWS Networking, the Backbone Enterprise, and Regional Engineering (BERE) organization is
responsible for the design, implementation, and operations of a wide array of networking infrastructure
that provide global connectivity between all AWS Regions and edge locations.
BERE provides the massive scale required to support our AWS customers and internal services, via a
network that experiences 70% growth annually. In addition, they have teams that are responsible for the design and operation of our global corporate office and Data Center network, allowing tens of thousands of Amazonians to perform their daily tasks in support of our customers.

AWS Global Connectivity and Network Availability (GCNA) Videos:
• Working at AWS in the GCNA Team - Meet Robert, VP: https://youtu.be/8v5i42FL02w
• Working at AWS in the GCNA Team - Meet Xiaonan, Sr. Systems Development Engineer: https://youtu.be/58Q1SyGZ4qg

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Dev Engineer, Benefits Experience and Technology (BXT)
jobs.description:
Using your benefits today means portals, phone calls, hold music, and fine print. We are changing that by bringing AI in as a strategic partner: software that understands what a person needs and helps them find the answer at the moment of need. This posting is for the tech lead on one of our two biggest product bets, driving large, ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations. This is a generative-AI and agentic-engineering role first, at very large scale.

You will join Benefits Engagement Technology and Services (BETS), the Amazon organization reinventing how more than a million employees and their families engage with their benefits. Our vision is benefits that are AI-powered, personalized, and proactive, where timely guidance reaches people when they need it rather than making them hunt for it. BETS builds and operates the platform that delivers benefits experiences across mobile, web, and an AI assistant, from self-service content creation to multi-channel campaigns to analytics, and we are now building a family of AI-native products on top of it.
Two of those products are our biggest bets, and we are building each as a focused product team inside BETS:
- A reimagined health plan where AI is a strategic partner for members instead of a portal to navigate. Rather than directories, phone trees, and hold music, it understands what someone needs and brings the right answer to them at the moment of need: the in-network doctor, the real out-of-pocket cost before they book, the claim explained in plain language, and the next step taken on their behalf. It is built on secure, HIPAA-compliant foundations to serve very large member populations, with a path to serve other organizations over time.
- An agentic workforce for benefits operations that makes running benefits for a workforce of millions dramatically easier. Managing dozens of programs, vendors, and budgets is enormous operational work; AI agents take on that heavy lifting, surfacing what needs attention, preparing the analysis and the recommended action, and handling the routine, so the people who manage benefits spend their time on decisions and strategy instead of manual operations. The system learns from every decision and keeps that knowledge with the team.

You will be the tech lead on one of these two products.

Here is what sets this organization apart: we do not just build AI products, we build them the AI Native way, and we have already proven it. A small pod rebuilt a major benefits platform and shipped it to production in 3 months, work originally scoped at 12, by restructuring how we engineer around agents. In our model, humans own judgment and agents own the mechanical middle. Engineers write the specification and set the acceptance criteria; agents (Claude Code, Kiro) write a growing share of the implementation, author tests, and resolve code-review comments; engineers direct, validate, and own what ships, and still hand-write the novel, ambiguous, and infrastructure-heavy work where models fall short. Recursive self-improvement, where the system proposes its own next version and a human approves, is the north star we are deliberately climbing toward, one validated step at a time, with humans at the judgment gates.

As a Senior Software Development Engineer in BETS, you are the tech lead for your team’s product. You lead the software development of a system of many features across its full lifecycle, working shoulder to shoulder with peers on related teams, on problems where the customer direction is clear but the technology strategy is not and the constraints conflict and span multiple organizations. You own the team-level architecture and provide the system-wide view and design guidance, making the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse decisions and reviewing others’ work, human-authored and agent-authored alike, so it fits the bigger picture and is extensible, performant, and secure. You stay hands-on in the code and code reviews that matter most.

You lead the team’s adoption and evolution of the AI Native build loops (the specs, acceptance criteria, and simulation coverage that let agents safely take on more of the work, plus the scoped authorization and guardrails that travel with that autonomy) and shape the agentic foundations the team builds on, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP. You drive operational excellence for a regulated, large-scale service, resolve root causes even when the fix crosses team boundaries, and are sought out by partner teams (identity, privacy, security, legal, and vendors) for your expertise. Above all, you grow the engineers around you: you lead through influence and constructive debate, coach and mentor multiple engineers, and set a quality bar the team emulates. The strongest technical leaders here work backwards from the customer and bring a strong product design sense, not just technical elegance, to every decision.

How we work, honestly: teams here are small, which means high ownership density and architectural decisions you will actually own rather than inherit fully formed. Some of our work carries hard, externally committed launch dates, so this role carries real deadline pressure. Because we handle sensitive personal data, privacy and security are designed in from the start and are everyone’s responsibility, not an afterthought. You own what you build, including its operations and on-call. In return you build rare, portable depth: regulated, large-scale platforms, production agentic systems, and the judgment to direct them.

This role is for tech leads who think like owners. If you want to prove that a small, senior team can enter a hard domain and win, if you want to design the systems that build systems, and if you are drawn to decisions that will still matter across the next several product generations, this is a rare seat.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead your team’s software development end to end: own the team-level architecture, provide the system-wide view and design guidance, make the high-stakes one-way-door decisions, and deliver a system of many features across its full lifecycle.
- Be the tech lead on large, ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations, where the customer direction is clear but the technology strategy is not; drive clarity and align partner teams (identity, privacy, security, legal, and vendors) on the path forward.
- Lead and mentor engineers: coach multiple engineers on and off your team, help grow the team through recruiting and career guidance, and drive adoption of engineering best practices that others emulate.
- Work backwards from the customer, bringing product design judgment to technical decisions, not just technical elegance.
- Lead the team’s AI Native build loops: define the specs, acceptance criteria, and simulation coverage that let agents safely take on more of the work, and shape the agentic foundations the team builds on (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, MCP).
- Stay a hands-on practitioner: contribute to the code and code reviews that most affect the product, and hold human-authored and agent-authored work to the same high bar.
- Drive operational excellence and resolve root causes across boundaries: ensure strong alarms, telemetry, runbooks, and retrospectives, and eliminate endemic problems even when the fix requires influencing other teams.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, AWS Networking: MONA
jobs.description:

We build the in-house software that solves our hardest network business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning systems. - Design and build the in-house systems that solve our business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning software — end-to-end, architected to scale with robust tests and metrics.
- Own and evolve our controller for agentic network auto-remediation that detects and resolves network issues automatically.
- Build the planning software that plans every new data center — capacity, racks, and ports — and deploys new network fabric.

jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.

If you're passionate about building robust, scalable software for complex robotic systems and want to work across the full robotics stack—from low-level system interfaces to high-level application logic—then we'd like to talk to you about becoming part of an organization with global impact on millions of customers.

Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate is enthusiastic about building the right solutions for our customers and will collaborate with other teams to ensure that our product meets Amazon-scale requirements. They will:
- Develop real-time sensor data processing pipelines, including implementing sensor fusion algorithms and computer vision models for robotic perception.
- Develop and optimize multi-modal data recording pipelines to support recording high-bandwidth data from multiple sensor sources simultaneously.
- Develop physics-realistic simulations of various sensor types (LiDAR, Radar, IMU, force/torque, tactile) to enable virtual testing and validation of perception and control algorithms prior to hardware deployment.
- Design, develop, and maintain production software for robotic systems in C++ and/or Python, spanning perception, motion planning, controls, and application layers.
