jobs.title: SDE- MES, Amazon Leo, Manufacturing Execution Systems
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we've designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The MES team is seeking a Software Development Engineer to design, develop, and deploy Manufacturing Execution System software that drives satellite production operations. You will build and maintain the core MES platform capabilities that manage work orders, process routing, data collection, traceability, and production analytics across Leo's manufacturing facilities.

You will work directly within the MES team to solve complex challenges related to production orchestration, shop floor system integrations, and real-time manufacturing data management. This is a hands-on development role focused on building the software systems that enable repeatable, controlled, and scalable manufacturing execution.

Export Control: This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop MES application features including work order management, process routing, recipe management, data collection, and product traceability.
- Build and maintain integrations between the MES platform and shop floor control systems (e.g., Ignition), enabling real-time production monitoring and machine-level data exchange.
- Develop integrations between MES and enterprise systems including ERP, PLM, and quality management platforms.
- Implement manufacturing process enforcement logic within MES to ensure production steps are executed in the correct sequence with proper validations.
- Build data pipelines and reporting capabilities within the MES ecosystem to support production analytics, yield tracking, and KPI dashboards.
- Develop and maintain MES APIs and services that enable production teams to manage and monitor manufacturing operations.
- Write clean, well-tested, production-quality code following MES team coding standards and best practices.
- Implement system monitoring, alerting, and observability for MES services to ensure uptime and rapid issue detection.
- Troubleshoot and resolve MES application issues in production environments, performing root cause analysis and implementing permanent fixes.
- Support MES system upgrades, version migrations, and configuration changes across production environments.
- Develop automated testing frameworks for MES features to ensure reliability during deployments and upgrades.
- Participate in MES design reviews, code reviews, and sprint planning to deliver capabilities on schedule and with high quality.
- Contribute to MES system documentation including architecture diagrams, runbooks, and operational procedures.
- Support UAT activities with manufacturing end-users and incorporate feedback into MES application improvements.
- Participate in on-call rotations to maintain MES system availability and respond to production incidents.

A day in the life
As a member of the MES team, your day revolves around building and supporting the software that production teams rely on daily to manufacture satellites. You will write code for MES features, review pull requests from teammates, and work with manufacturing engineers who use the system to understand their pain points and requirements.

A typical day involves developing new MES capabilities (e.g., a new process routing workflow or integration endpoint), debugging production issues that affect manufacturing operations, participating in team standups and sprint ceremonies, and collaborating with MES TPMs and manufacturing stakeholders on upcoming feature priorities.

You should be comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where system availability directly impacts production output, and where requirements evolve as production processes mature and scale.

About the team
The MES team builds and maintains the Manufacturing Execution System that powers Leo's satellite production operations. The team is responsible for the core MES platform — including work order management, process routing, data collection, traceability, and production reporting — as well as all integrations between MES and shop floor control systems like Ignition, ERP, PLM, and quality management systems.

The team's mission is to deliver a reliable, scalable MES platform that enables manufacturing teams to execute controlled, repeatable production processes while maintaining rigorous data integrity and compliance standards across Leo's internal facilities and contract manufacturing sites.

The MES team operates in Bellevue, WA, and works closely with manufacturing operations teams in Redmond and Kirkland, WA.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Amazon Shipping
jobs.description:
You will build the optimization brain for Amazon's externalized logistics network — a system that couples first-mile route planning with middle-mile network optimization into a joint iterative loop, producing end-to-end recommendations that no single optimizer can reach alone. The technical challenge is real: solvers that take hours per run, a combinatorial search space that defies brute-force, model gaps that require deep-diving into solver internals, and convergence that must be proven across independently owned engines. This is not a scale or latency problem — it's a multi-system optimization convergence problem where you invent the pruning, approximation, and coupling strategies. Your recommendations will directly shape commercial decisions — which shippers to pursue, which geographies to grow, which contracts to reprice — giving this role rare direct business impact for a PE position.

In addition, you will provide tech leadership to the fulfillment charter for Amazon Shipping where you will be responsible for increasing the label conversion rates that would be a key enabler for revenue growth; identify solutions such as dynamic network capacity management to build a resilient network topology; identify and build speed opportunities in the upstream planning systems; and solve unique challenges related to delivery addresses for an externalized supply chain business where orders are created outside amazon marketplace.

You will also be responsible for architectural integrity and scalability of fulfillment systems by (1) identifying interface contracts with partner tech teams (2) making the architecture more nimble and self-serve for faster time-to-market of new capabilities (3) improving resiliency and availability of Tier-1 systems (4) optimizing the level of service orchestration within the fulfillment systems.


Key job responsibilities
• Architect the joint FM-MM optimization loop: state-passing contracts, convergence detection, parallel execution, and checkpoint/restart
• Solve computational tractability through smart pruning, lightweight solvers, and metaheuristic search at network scale
• Drive cross-org alignment across 5+ organizations — securing stable interfaces and committed roadmap items
• Translate optimization outputs into actionable recommendations for Operations (node mapping, capacity), Commercial (shipper targets, geographies), and Finance (cost-to-serve, contract economics)
• Mentor a team of Applied Scientists and SDEs; set technical bar and build experimentation culture
• Define and execute the phased roadmap: FM cost optimizer (Phase 1) → joint FM-MM optimizer (Phase 2) → decision engines that close the loop from network optimization to commercial strategy (Phase 3)
• Own system validation and accuracy: design feedback loops from actual vs. predicted outcomes, detect degradation, and define refresh cadence

This is deep systems work: you will shape the runtime, the communication layer, and the protocol integrations that everything else in the platform is built on.


In this role you will:
Design and build real-time middleware and runtime components — the data-exchange layer, type system, and communication patterns (publish/subscribe and request/reply) that connect distributed control applications across languages and hardware.

Integrate with industrial automation platforms and hardware protocols (e.g. IEC 61131-3, EtherCAT, PROFINET, Modbus, OPC-UA, IO-Link) and the device drivers that bridge them onto the platform.

Build the bridge to the cloud — reliable metric publication, command handling, and telemetry from the edge into AWS, with the right delivery guarantees for each data class.

Work at the boundary of distributed and real-time systems, where correctness means both the right result and the right timing — bounded latency, predictable behavior, and graceful degradation when connectivity is lost.

Partner with a cross-functional team of hardware engineers, controls engineers, data center operations, and security specialists to take features from design through to hardware validation.

If you're excited by low-level systems, real-time data movement, and connecting physical equipment to the cloud at scale, this is the role for you.

Architecting and implementing runtime and real-time middleware — high-performance, low-latency components that run both on embedded/edge controllers and in the cloud, with a focus on determinism, reliability, and resource efficiency on constrained hardware.

Building industrial protocol and hardware integrations — extending the platform with new device drivers and protocol support and solving the hard problems of cross-language, cross-platform data exchange (type systems, serialization, memory layout, and schema/versioning).

Owning the edge-to-cloud communication path — designing how telemetry, metrics, and commands flow between devices and AWS services with appropriate quality-of-service, backpressure, and store-and-forward behavior.

Engineering for real-time correctness — reasoning about latency budgets, throughput, and failure modes in a distributed system where the software is adjacent to physical control loops.

Collaborating across disciplines—working with hardware, controls, security, and operations partners to turn ambiguous requirements into robust, shippable software.

Mentoring and contributing to technical direction — guiding more junior engineers and helping shape the roadmap for the runtime and middleware layer.

The ideal candidate has a strong systems-software background and experience across several of the following: real-time or embedded systems, industrial automation platforms and hardware protocols, distributed systems, middleware/messaging (pub/sub, RPC), and cloud communication. You are comfortable working close to the metal, memory, concurrency, and serialization timing and equally comfortable reasoning about how edge components integrate with cloud services. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to correctness in the face of hardware and timing constraints, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment are essential. jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, MONA
jobs.description:
AWS runs one of the largest networks in the world, and MONA (Management, Out-of-Band Networks, and Automation) alone owns over one million physical devices across its full lifecycle. We are in the critical path for every new data center powering the AI revolution.

We build the in-house software that solves our hardest network business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning systems. For example, we own a controller for agentic network auto-remediation, and the planning software that plans every new data center down to capacity and ports. We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to be a technical leader and force multiplier: you will partner with the engineering manager to shape our software strategy while continuing to design and build these systems at fleet scale. If you want the scope to influence what we build and how we build it — and to keep building it yourself — this is that role.


Key job responsibilities
- Partner with the engineering manager to shape the team's software strategy — architecture, roadmap, and long-term vision — for the in-house systems behind a 1M+ device network (everything we run, we build ourselves).
- Design and build the in-house systems that solve our business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning software — end-to-end, architected to scale with robust tests and metrics.
- Own and evolve our controller for agentic network auto-remediation that detects and resolves network issues automatically.
- Build the planning software that plans every new data center — capacity, racks, and ports — and deploys new network fabric.
- Own out-of-band management-plane services: serial console access to every server and router, plus managed connectivity such as SSH.
- Drive correctness and safety for automation acting on production networks: idempotency, guardrails, and observability that proves work actually happened.
- Lead design reviews, raise the operational-excellence and code-quality bar, and mentor engineers.
- Participate in on-call and help lead high-severity incident response.


A day in the life
No two days look the same. One morning you are whiteboarding with the manager and a principal engineer on how to evolve the control plane for the next wave of AI data centers; the next you are deep in a greenfield auto-remediation service that resolves faults automatically instead of paging a human at 3am. You will make a teammate's design better, unblock a data-center build with capacity planning, and harden out-of-band console access to a million devices. You will see your work land at a scale almost nowhere else can offer — with real autonomy and teammates sharp enough to make you better.

About the team
MONA (Management, Out-of-Band Networks, and Automation) is part of AWS Core Networking. We are a highly motivated team of software, systems, and network developers who thrive on solving challenging problems and building large-scale distributed systems. AWS runs one of the largest networks in the world, and MONA alone owns the full lifecycle of over a million physical devices — driving new innovation in one of the largest data center networks on Earth. Everything we run we build in-house: controllers, software-defined networking, planning software, etc.

jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer, AI Studios Engineering

Design, develop, and maintain software components for our AI-native content creation platform, supporting professional animation and live action/VFX workflows Implement features across the stack—from backend services, media processing pipelines, and APIs to ML model integrations and creator-facing tooling—with guidance from senior engineers Write clean, well-tested, and maintainable code while participating in code reviews to both give and receive constructive feedback Collaborate with cross-functional teams including ML scientists, applied scientists, product managers, and creative professionals to understand requirements and deliver solutions Contribute to integrations with industry-standard Digital Content Creation (DCC) tools such as Adobe Animate, After Effects, Maya, and Storyboard Pro Troubleshoot and debug issues in production systems, contributing to operational excellence and system reliability Participate in on-call rotations and contribute to improving system monitoring, alerting, and documentation Continuously learn new technologies, tools, and methodologies relevant to AI/ML systems, media processing, and distributed computing

A day in the life
As an SDE on the AI Studios team, you'll spend most of your time writing and reviewing code, with regular opportunities to collaborate with teammates on design discussions. A typical day might include building API endpoints for our creator tooling platform, implementing new features for our live action VFX pipeline, or debugging an integration with our proprietary AI models. What makes this role unique is the opportunity to work on-site alongside VFX artists and creative professionals, sitting with them as they use your tools, watching where workflows break down, and iterating rapidly to meet the demands of production timelines. You'll participate in team standups, sprint planning, and retrospectives while building your understanding of our systems. You'll have opportunities to learn from experienced engineers and gradually take on more complex challenges as you grow, all while working on technology that powers content featuring world-class IPs.

About the team

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Fulfillment by Amazon, FBA

We are building a team dedicated to solving these category-level structural barriers — redesigning fee architectures, building new fulfillment capabilities, closing cost-to-serve gaps against 3PLs, and earning seller trust at price points where every defect matters. This is a multi-year charter with leadership alignment, end-to-end ownership, and the mandate to work across organizational boundaries to deliver what no single team has been able to solve alone.

We operate with startup intensity inside Amazon — small teams, fast cycles, and the freedom to invent. Come build the systems that unlock FBA's biggest untapped opportunities.

Key job responsibilities
As an SDE-2 on this team, you will be a technical leader who owns the design and delivery of systems at the intersection of seller economics, fulfillment infrastructure, and category-specific growth:

- Design and build end-to-end systems that remove structural barriers to FBA adoption.
- Own the technical architecture for your domain, balancing speed-to-market with long-term scalability across FBA's global footprint
- Work across organizational boundaries — our charter includes alignment to make changes on partner teams' systems where needed to deliver the mission

jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer – AI/ML Networking Disaggregated Inference, Annapurna Labs, Annapurna Labs
jobs.description:
Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds.

We're looking for an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the absolute limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll own pieces of the high-speed transfer path that make the difference, and you'll measure your success in how close you run to the theoretical peak of the machine.

In this role you will:

Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric.
Push performance to the hardware roofline: profile, find the real bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs as fast as physics permits."
Work across the stack — from kernel and network transport up to the inference frameworks — and partner with teams building the chips, runtime, and models.
Deliver features that run on our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production.
What we're looking for:

Strong C/C++ and a love for low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, kernels, memory, and writing fast code.
The instinct to ask "how fast could this possibly go?" and the rigor to measure it.
Experience with high-speed networking or HPC interconnects (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NIXL, MPI) is valued highly; embedded-systems experience is a plus.
Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required — if you're a great systems engineer, we'll teach you the ML side.
If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working shoulder-to-shoulder with HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. This is a role on the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure.

About the team: You'd be joining Annapurna Labs, an integral part of AWS. Annapurna designs the hardware and software building blocks behind EC2 — every EC2 instance runs on hardware we designed. We specialize in the chips, systems, and software that optimize the AWS customer experience, and this team sits where cutting-edge AI meets the silicon and the network underneath it.

A day in the life
Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS.

We have mixed discipline orgs, you’d be working side by side with infrastructure experts, hardware engineers, RTL engineers, scientists & architects. Our workforce spans the globe and is truly international, you’ll find yourself working side by side with individuals from numerous countries. We take mentorship seriously, you can both expect senior mentorship and will be expected to mentor new and junior engineers.

The pace is fast as we work on the latest advancements of AI/ML, but we take the time to bond as a team and enjoy the successes. We offer flexibility in working hours, and respect WLB as a core org tenet. The team enjoys working with numerous principal-level engineers and closely with directors, career growth opportunities are certainly available. This is a role where you will always be encouraged to keep learning, the AI/ML field is fast moving and constantly evolving.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer, SIEGE

jobs.title: SDE II - Network Observability, Leo Networking Software
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s Low Earth Orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team builds the systems that provide deep, end-to-end insight into the health, performance, and reliability of this global telecom network. Our systems span the full Leo service—from satellites and customer terminals to ground gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial network infrastructure—and enable engineers to understand network behavior, rapidly detect failures, and diagnose complex issues across space and ground infrastructure.
We are looking for a talented Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate network observability and analytics solutions for an advanced global telecommunications service spanning both space and terrestrial networks.

As a software engineer on this team, you will build high-scale systems that transform telemetry, network events, traces, and operational signals into actionable visibility. You will work across distributed systems, networking, data pipelines, real-time analytics, and visualization to answer critical questions such as: Is the network healthy? Where is a failure occurring? What is its customer impact? And how quickly can we identify and resolve it?
You will collaborate closely with network engineers, scientists, and software engineers to develop novel mechanisms for end-to-end network visibility and diagnostics. Your work will help establish the observability foundations required to operate a highly distributed telecom network where failures can span satellites, beams, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop highly scalable network observability, telemetry, and analytics systems spanning space and terrestrial infrastructure.
- Build real-time and near-real-time pipelines that ingest and correlate high-volume network telemetry, events, traces, and health signals.
- Develop algorithms and services that provide end-to-end network visibility, including failure detection, localization, correlation, and impact analysis.
- Build tools and platforms that enable engineers to quickly understand network health and diagnose complex, multi-hop failures.
- Design distributed systems capable of processing large volumes of telemetry while maintaining high availability, durability, and low latency.
- Develop APIs, services, dashboards, and analytical tools that expose network health and operational insights to internal customers.
- Work closely with network engineers and scientists to translate complex networking problems into robust software solutions.
- Establish metrics, service-level indicators, and automated detection mechanisms for critical Leo network components.
- Design systems that remain resilient in the presence of intermittent connectivity, partial failures, delayed telemetry, and unreliable network paths.
- Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support.
- Drive technical decisions across team boundaries and contribute to engineering standards for observability, reliability, and operational excellence.
- Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software development.


A day in the life
You will work on problems at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, telemetry, and large-scale analytics. One day you might design a streaming architecture capable of processing telemetry from millions of network components; another day you might develop a mechanism to identify where packet loss occurred across a multi-hop satellite and terrestrial path.
You will work with network engineers and scientists to understand how Leo’s network behaves, develop new ways to make that behavior observable, and turn large volumes of operational data into actionable information. You will also own services in production and work through real operational challenges as the network scales.
This role provides opportunities to work across the stack—from telemetry collection on network infrastructure and embedded systems, through distributed data pipelines and analytics, to the APIs and visualization tools used by engineers operating the Leo network.



About the team
The Leo Network Observability, Visibility & Analytics team is responsible for making a highly distributed global telecom network understandable and operable at scale.
We build the visibility layer that connects network signals across satellites, customer terminals, gateways, cloud services, and terrestrial infrastructure. Our systems help transform individual telemetry signals into an end-to-end view of network health, enabling faster detection, diagnosis, and resolution of issues.
The problems we solve are inherently distributed and require us to combine software engineering with networking and data science. We are building new capabilities rather than simply applying existing observability patterns to a conventional cloud service.
If you enjoy solving ambiguous problems, designing distributed systems at significant scale, and building software that provides visibility into complex networks, this team offers an opportunity to work on foundational systems for Amazon Leo.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Device Cloud Core Services
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Sr. Embedded Engineer, Amazon Robotics
jobs.description:

Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate is enthusiastic and passionate about building the right solutions for our customers and willing to work with other teams to ensure that our product will meet Amazon-scale while simultaneously raising the bar for associate's safety. They will:

jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. As an engineer, you will have the opportunity to work on challenging problems in the low-latency/high-throughput domain of dynamic ad insertion. The systems you design and build will be in the core path of video delivery to Prime Video customers worldwide, operating at a scale where a single live event can reach tens of millions of concurrent viewers with zero tolerance for disruption. We leverage Amazon Web Services (AWS) technologies including AWS CloudFront, EC2, S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, SNS, SQS and internal AWS incubator technologies.

You will need to have an established background in developing customer-facing experiences, a strong technical ability, great communication skills, a motivation to achieve results in a fast-paced environment, a high level of creativity and great analytical reasoning skills.

Key job responsibilities
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Experience with critical, 24x7 systems

Prime Video Ads team's mission is to build a seamless ad delivery, playback and reporting experience across all supported PV devices. PV Ads team owns services for ad ingestion, ad stitching and integrates with ad decision systems. Its services handle dynamic transcoding and ad insertions as part of video playback.

The team is chartered to design large scale systems to power the live and vod streams with ads viewed by a massive audience daily, and you will help bring customers streaming video view experience to a new level. jobs.title: Sr Software Development Engineer, Software Defined Network Agent
jobs.description:

As a Senior Software Development Engineer on the Software Defined Networking (SDN) Control Plane team, you will lead the design and development of the Agents that runs in all the devices including satellites, customer terminals, gateways, and terrestrial infrastructure to drive network plans. About the team
The SDN Control Plane team builds and operates the brain of the Leo network. jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Prime Video Offers Expansion
jobs.description:
Behind every "Buy," "Rent," "Subscribe," or "Bundle" button on Prime Video is a decision our system made in milliseconds: what offer to show, at what price, with what promotions, for which customer, in which country. We own that decision.

Our team within Prime Video Commerce owns critical offer orchestration and pricing services that power the global commerce experience. Our systems determine pricing, apply promotions, compose bundles, and serve the right offer to the right customer across every Prime Video surface. We process millions of requests per second, operate across 100+ markets, and sit on the critical path for every Prime Video transaction worldwide, spanning subscriptions, rentals, purchases, channels, and bundles.

The challenge is not scale alone. It is scale plus rapid change. We are expanding into dozens of new marketplaces each year, each with unique payment methods, regulatory requirements, and pricing models. We are building dynamic pricing capabilities, enabling promotional experiences for major commercial events, and evolving how offers are composed as the product portfolio grows. Every new market and every new offer type adds combinatorial complexity to a system that must remain correct, fast, and available.

We are looking for a Senior SDE who wants to own hard problems in a system where getting it wrong means a customer sees the wrong price, cannot complete their purchase, or misses an offer they should have seen. You will own services end-to-end, make architectural calls, ship to production, and operate what you build. The work is technical, the impact is immediate, and the problems do not come pre-solved.

Key job responsibilities
- Own and evolve offer orchestration and pricing services that determine what customers see globally, making architecture decisions for correctness, latency, and resilience
- Design systems that handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-market, multi-currency, multi-promotion offer serving at millions of TPS
- Investigate and resolve production issues that cross service boundaries, often requiring deep analysis of traffic patterns, caching behavior, and downstream dependencies to find non-obvious root causes
- Drive marketplace expansion from an engineering perspective: configuration, offer distribution, compliance requirements, and end-to-end validation across new territories
- Build and maintain operational health for Tier-1 services: stress testing, capacity planning, alarm tuning, scaling strategies, and incident prevention
- Propose and drive architectural improvements that reduce operational toil, improve system reliability, or eliminate classes of production defects, without waiting to be asked
- Provide technical leadership through design reviews, code reviews, and architecture guidance, helping engineers across the team make better decisions and grow in scope
- Leverage AI tooling strategically to accelerate engineering workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and improve development velocity while maintaining quality and ownership of all design decisions


A day in the life
One morning you are tracing why an offer disappeared for customers in a specific region, following the data flow through multiple services until you find the filtering logic that does not account for a lifecycle edge case. The next day you are designing how a new promotional pricing type should propagate through the offer pipeline without breaking existing business rules. Later in the week you are reviewing stress test results, comparing actual traffic distribution against test configurations, and filing a scaling request based on your analysis. On Friday you are pairing with a newer engineer on their first multi-market configuration change, helping them understand the compliance implications before they ship.

The work moves between deep technical investigation, system design, production operations, and people development. You will not do the same thing two days in a row.

About the team
We are part of the Prime Video Commerce organization, based in Bengaluru. We own services that power offer serving, pricing, and commerce experiences for customers globally. Our scope spans pricing and promotions, offer composition, bundling, and international expansion across dozens of markets.

We work as part of a global engineering organization with counterparts across multiple locations and time zones. We respect time zones, value directness, and believe that the best engineering happens when people feel ownership over their domain and trust within their team. We are a high-ownership team where individual contributions are visible and impactful.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, SageMaker Compute Governance
jobs.description:
Training and running large AI models takes enormous amounts of expensive accelerated compute, and most of it sits idle. Across the industry, a large share of GPU capacity is paid for but never does useful work because jobs cannot find it, cannot share it, or cannot see it and use it efficiently. We build the services that closes that gap.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build the systems that put idle or inefficiently used GPUs to work. You will design and build distributed backend services that let organizations pool capacity across many clusters and accounts, route it to the workloads that need it most, and see exactly how it is being used. This is deep systems work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, container orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, and it directly changes how much value customers get from every GPU they pay for.

You will own services end to end, from design through launch and operation in production, and your work will ship to some of the largest AI compute customers in the world.

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate distributed backend services that manage and share accelerated compute across multiple clusters and accounts.

Build scheduling and capacity-sharing capabilities that move compute to the highest-priority workloads and reclaim it when priorities change.

Build zero-touch usage and guidance systems that collect, aggregate, and report how compute is consumed, at scale and in near real time.

Own your services in production: define operational metrics, respond to issues, and continuously improve reliability, latency, and cost.

Write clear design documents, participate in design and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar for the team.

Collaborate with product, design, and partner engineering teams to turn customer problems into shipped features.

Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of ownership, quality, and customer focus.

A day in the life
Most days start with a short team stand-up, then it is mostly building. You might design a service that lets one cluster borrow idle capacity from another, then write it up for a design review where the team pokes holes in it before any code is written. Hard problems get their own deep-dive whiteboard session. Other days lean toward operations, chasing down why a workload did not get the capacity it should have. You will not be handed fully specified tasks; you will have the independence to help decide what to build, then build it.

About the team
We help customers get the most out of the accelerated compute they pay for. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure every accelerator a customer pays for is doing useful work, and make that easy to see and control. Cost reduction is one important part of that, but the bigger idea is the engine that delivers compute to the workloads that need it most, in as little time as possible.

Our customers run some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world, and they feel the impact of our work directly in how much they can do with their infrastructure. We care about depth, we own our work end to end, and we build in the open where we can.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer , Amazon Customer Service
jobs.description:
Customer experience is at the heart of all we do at Amazon, as we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Amazon Customer Service (CS) is at the forefront of customer experience, working relentlessly to provide customers a convenient, high quality, and delightful experience across all of our CS channels in every interaction.

Within CS, Network Solutions is responsible for designing, planning, and operating the world's largest customer service network - building intelligent, adaptive systems that anticipate demand, match customers to optimal experiences, and continuously improve service quality. We are seeking a Sr. Software Development Engineer to lead the engineering team building the Network Control Center (NCC) - an AI-native system that will transform how Amazon detects, responds to, and recovers from incidents across our global Customer Service network. Today, our incident management relies on disconnected tools, multiple manual steps, and reactive detection that takes several minutes. This leader will design and build the technical systems that replace this fragmented approach with continuous observability, autonomous response, and intelligent customer recovery — all operating in real-time at massive scale.

The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader who thrives in ambiguity, can translate a bold vision into a concrete system architecture, and is passionate about building high-performing teams. You will partner closely with science, product, and operations leaders to deliver AI-powered capabilities that detect risks before customers feel them, respond in sub-60 seconds, and execute tailored recovery actions that turn service failures into loyalty-building moments. This is an exciting opportunity to build transformative technology that directly impacts the experience of millions of customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead the design, architecture, and delivery of an AI-native observability and incident management service serving Amazon's global Customer Service network
- Build and develop a high-performing engineering team by assisting in hiring and mentoring software development engineers
- Architect real-time signal detection and observability systems that continuously monitor network health, identifying risks and anomalies before customer impact
- Deliver autonomous incident response and recovery capabilities that replace manual, fragmented processes with intelligent, real-time intervention

- Establish operational excellence practices for production services, including on-call, incident response, and continuous improvement mechanisms

About the team
Network Solutions is on a mission to transform Amazon Customer Service from a cost center into a growth driver by building intelligent, adaptive systems that anticipate demand, match customers to optimal experiences, and continuously improve service quality. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Identity
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Transactional Services
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, EC2 Nitro, EC2 Local Instance Store
jobs.description:

jobs.title: SDE, Responsible AI
jobs.description:
AI is transforming every corner of Amazon — and with that transformation comes the responsibility to get it right. The Amazon Responsible AI (RAI) team is building the systems that ensure Amazon's AI is fair, safe, transparent, and compliant with emerging global regulations. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who wants to work at the frontier of AI governance — building the platform that gives Amazon real-time visibility into the compliance posture of thousands of AI systems across the company.

No one has solved AI governance at this scale before. Today, tracking thousands of AI systems against evolving regulatory frameworks, internal expectations, and voluntary commitments is a problem that's impossible to manage manually. You'll build the platform that makes it possible — automating what would take an army of auditors, and giving builders the tools to do the right thing without slowing down. This is a greenfield opportunity on a small, senior team building from scratch alongside Amazon Scholars, Principal Applied Scientists, and policy experts. You'll own the architecture and shape the product direction.

As an SDE on the Responsible AI team, you will design and build systems that discover AI workloads across Amazon's fleet, classify them against regulatory risk frameworks, streamline compliance evidence collection through paved-path tooling, and surface actionable insights to both builders and leadership. You'll collaborate closely with Applied Scientists developing AI-powered classification agents, privacy engineers, and policy experts navigating a rapidly evolving regulatory landscape.

This role is for builders who are energized by ambiguity, excited to define the technical direction of a new product, and motivated by the societal impact of ensuring AI systems are developed responsibly.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and operate distributed services that automatically discover and catalog AI systems across Amazon's infrastructure
- Build classification and risk-assessment pipelines that map AI systems to regulatory frameworks and internal compliance requirements
- Develop self-service tooling and paved-path integrations that help builder teams demonstrate conformance with responsible AI expectations
- Build the infrastructure that hosts and scales ML-powered compliance workflows developed by our Applied Science team
- Partner with Privacy, Legal, and RAI Science to translate evolving regulatory requirements into scalable technical solutions
- Maintain a high operational excellence bar for systems that inform regulatory reporting timelines

About the team
Amazon Responsible AI works to maximize the benefits and minimize the risks of AI technology across Amazon. We define responsible AI through core dimensions — Fairness, Safety, Privacy, Security, Veracity, Robustness, Explainability, Transparency, Controllability, and Governance — and we build the tools and programs that help Amazon's builder teams deliver on those dimensions at scale. Our team includes Applied Scientists, Amazon Scholars, Security Engineers, TPMs, and SDEs. We are science-led, independent advisors — and we're building the next generation of AI governance infrastructure from the ground up.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer III, AWS Transactional Services (Database & Distributed Systems)
jobs.description:

The Transactional Services organization builds foundational distributed systems that power some of AWS's largest services. We specialize in high-performance, strongly consistent data systems operating at massive scale. Today, our systems process more than 4 million writes per second, and that scale continues to grow. The systems we build sit on critical paths for AWS, so the work has broad technical and customer impact.

Our team is executing on a multi-year roadmap of complex, high-impact engineering work. We are investing in an already high-performing storage layer to drive even lower latency, higher availability, and new capabilities for customers at scale. This is an opportunity to work on foundational systems with meaningful headroom for innovation in performance, efficiency, and reliability.

As a Senior Software Development Engineer, you will be a technical leader within the team, helping drive the design and delivery of our most important engineering work. You will partner closely with your manager and Principal Engineers to translate roadmap goals into executable technical plans, raise engineering quality, and mentor other engineers on the team. This role is well suited for someone who combines strong distributed systems design skills with sound engineering judgment, consistent execution, and a willingness to help the broader team succeed.

If you want to lead the evolution of distributed systems at AWS scale, this is the role.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead the design and architecture of highly available, low-latency distributed log and database systems that support critical AWS services.
- Own complex and ambiguous technical problems end to end, from framing the problem and defining the approach to driving delivery into production.
- Set technical direction across foundational services, making architecture decisions that balance performance, durability, availability, and operational simplicity.
- Work with partner teams on shared designs and dependencies to ensure successful delivery of team-owned initiatives.
- Mentor and develop engineers through design reviews, code reviews, and hands-on technical guidance, helping raise the bar across the team.
- Advance engineering excellence by improving operational rigor, strengthening development practices, and shaping the team's technical culture.


About the team
WS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and continue to innovate, which is why customers ranging from startups to Global 500 companies trust our products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
At AWS, learning and curiosity are part of how we work. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion and help us celebrate different perspectives and experiences. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - AWS, Amazon GuardDuty
jobs.description:
Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors, analyzes, and processes AWS data sources and logs to identify unexpected, potentially unauthorized, and malicious activity within customer AWS environments. GuardDuty combines machine learning, anomaly detection, and malicious file discovery, using both AWS and third-party sources to help protect workloads and data across AWS accounts.

Amazon GuardDuty is seeking talented Software Development Engineers to join a team in our Los Angeles office!. In this role, you will design, build, and operate highly available, scalable distributed systems that power GuardDuty's Malware protection and Runtime Monitoring products. You will work on challenging problems at the intersection of cloud security, distributed systems, and customer experience — building platforms that serve both internal teams and millions of external AWS customers.

You will be a hands-on engineer contributing to the full software development lifecycle — from requirements gathering and system design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations. You will collaborate closely with security engineers, applied scientists, and product managers to deliver features that protect millions of AWS customers. This is a high-impact role where your work directly contributes to the security posture of AWS customers worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and maintain highly available, scalable distributed systems for GuardDuty's Malware Protection and Runtime Monitoring services
- Build and operate metadata services that enrich data for internal GuardDuty teams
- Own and evolve the runtime agent provisioning and agent coverage platform across AWS compute services
- Own features end-to-end across the full software development lifecycle — from design through deployment and operations
- Effectively leverage AI-assisted development tooling to accelerate design, coding, testing, code review, and operational workflows while maintaining a high quality bar
- Write high-quality, testable code and participate in design and code reviews, using AI tooling to improve velocity and consistency without compromising correctness or security
- Troubleshoot and resolve complex production issues, driving root cause analysis and operational excellence — including using AI tooling to accelerate log analysis, hypothesis generation, and runbook execution
- Collaborate with security engineers, applied scientists, and product managers to define technical solutions
- Mentor junior engineers on engineering best practices, including responsible and effective use of AI tooling, and contribute to team-wide standards
- Contribute to operational excellence through on-call rotations, runbook development, and system monitoring

A day in the life
As an SDE II on this team, you spend your time designing, building, and operating distributed systems that protect AWS customers from runtime threats at massive scale.

On any given day, you might be drafting a design document for a new feature, diving deep into code, reviewing a teammate's pull request, or debugging a production issue - using AI tooling along the way to move faster without cutting corners on quality.

You collaborate with security engineers, applied scientists, and product managers to understand their needs and build the right solutions. You participate in operational reviews, contribute to sprint planning, and mentor teammates as part of how the team operates.

The work is varied, fast-paced, and high-impact - every line of code you ship helps protect AWS customers.

About the team
Our team owns two of GuardDuty's core threat detection products: Malware Protection, which scans EC2 workloads, S3 objects for malicious files and supporting AWS Backup and Runtime Monitoring, which uses an eBPF agent to detect threats in real time across EC2, ECS, Fargate, and EKS.
We work at the intersection of security research, distributed systems, and operating system internals - protecting AWS customers from the threats that target their compute and data.

jobs.title: SDE, Alexa For Shopping
jobs.description:
What if you could talk to your Amazon Store? With Alexa+ on Echo Show, customers can now do exactly that. The full Amazon store is live on Echo Show 15 and 21 — a new way to shop at home that combines voice as a natural way to express needs with the product details, reviews, and videos customers rely on to make confident decisions.

This product started with an ambitious question and was built from scratch — no prior version to iterate on, no existing architecture to extend, no playbook to follow. The team pioneered novel challenges including rendering the full, always-current Amazon store natively on Echo Show in real time, building visual grounding from scratch so Alexa's responses stay anchored to what the customer sees on screen, and creating a conversational commerce paradigm that lets customers skip screens entirely with natural language.

We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to help build the next chapter of this experience — scaling what we've built, expanding to new surfaces and marketplaces, and pushing the boundaries of agentic, multimodal shopping. As an early-career engineer on this team, you'll design and build meaningful components alongside experienced engineers, own your work through design, implementation, testing, and livesite, and grow quickly in a high-ownership environment.

This is greenfield, 0→1 work at the intersection of Generative AI, multimodal experiences, and conversational commerce. You will have the freedom to experiment, learn, and invent on behalf of our customers, and you'll work for a strong leadership team that optimizes for your growth and pairs you with mentors who will guide your career.

Key job responsibilities
As a Software Development Engineer I on this team, you will:

- Design, build, test, and operate features that scale and extend the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices.

- Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate actively in code reviews, both giving and receiving thoughtful feedback.

- Contribute to systems that render the Amazon store in real time, keep it in sync, and support conversational, multimodal shopping flows.

- Help extend the experience to new surfaces and international marketplaces, working through ambiguity where there is no existing playbook.

- Own your components end-to-end through livesite operations — monitoring, on-call participation, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance.

- Collaborate with engineering, science, product, and design partners across Alexa Shopping, including teammates in Seattle across time zones.

- Contribute ideas to technical designs, ask good questions, and grow your scope and autonomy over time with support from senior engineers and mentors.

A day in the life
Here's what a typical day might look like. You'll spend meaningful time building — designing and implementing features that scale the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices, whether that's improving how the store renders in real time, sharpening visual grounding, or extending the experience to a new marketplace. You'll write code, review your teammates', and get thoughtful feedback on yours.

Days blend focused coding with a short standup, design conversations where your ideas are genuinely wanted, and pairing with a senior engineer or mentor when you're working through something ambiguous. Because this is 0→1 work, you'll often be making decisions without a playbook — and that's the fun part. You'll partner closely with engineering, science, product, and design colleagues across Alexa Shopping, many of them in Seattle, so some collaboration spans time zones.

Your internal stakeholders are the product, design, and partner engineering teams shaping the Alexa+ shopping experience; your end customers are shoppers at home talking to their Echo Show, expecting it to just work. The problems you'll tackle range from "how do we keep the store always in sync and fast on-device?" to "how do we make a conversational shopping flow feel effortless?" — meaty, customer-facing problems where what you build lands in people's living rooms.

About the team
We're the team that taught the Amazon Store to talk back. We took an idea that didn't have a blueprint and shipped it to customers' living rooms — and now we're just getting to the fun part: making it bigger, faster, and available to shoppers around the world.

Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make shopping on Alexa feel effortless and delightful, no matter where a customer is or which device they reach for. We sit right where voice, vision, and Generative AI meet retail at Amazon scale — which means the problems we solve genuinely haven't been solved before, and the person who cracks them is often the newest engineer with a fresh idea.

Culture-wise, we're builders who like ambiguity and dislike bureaucracy. We ship, we learn, we tell stories over chai, and we celebrate the wins (and the instructive failures). We hire smart people and give them room to run — you'll own real problems from day one, with experienced engineers and mentors in your corner, not looking over your shoulder. We take the work seriously and ourselves a little less so. If you like the idea of building something customers can literally talk to, you'll fit right in.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core
jobs.description:
Build the service that checks the health of millions of endpoints around the world every few seconds, and the consoles customers rely on to run DNS and route traffic at global scale. As an SDE on the Amazon Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core team, you will own the distributed health checking infrastructure and the public API in front of it, build the AI tooling every Route 53 service team depends on, and launch new AI services for DNS and Route 53. You will help define what our customers use next.

We are based in Vancouver, BC. We own Route 53 Health Checks, a highly available endpoint monitoring service that helps Route 53 DNS, Amazon Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon RDS, Amazon S3, and many other AWS services maintain high availability for their customers. We also own the core tooling, standards, and shared infrastructure that every Route 53 console is built on. This is a full stack role. You will design and operate the services and APIs behind Route 53 Health Checks, and you will take our console tooling from something our team uses to something every Route 53 service team builds on, while we hold the quality bar on what ships. Your work will reach across more than 10 service teams and the product managers, designers, and engineers you partner with throughout AWS networking. AI is central to how we work and what we build, from the tools we use to ship faster to the intelligent features we put in front of customers.

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate the distributed health checking infrastructure and public API behind Route 53 Health Checks.

Build and vend the AI tooling that service teams across Route 53 use to design and build their own console changes, and hold the quality bar on what they ship.

Own and build new AI services and capabilities for DNS and Route 53, from idea to launch.

Bring the latest AI tools and techniques into how the team designs, builds, and ships software.

Operate what you build. Take part in on call, own metrics and alarms, and drive root cause analysis on production issues.

Work with product managers, designers, and engineers across more than 10 service teams in AWS networking.

Turn requirements that are ambiguous and change quickly into products customers rely on.

Our health checking stack is primarily Java and Linux, with lots of interaction with public AWS services and Amazon internal tools. Our console stack is TypeScript and React. We do not expect you to know all of it, but we do expect you to be excited to learn it.

A day in the life
Our customers are the developers and businesses who use Route 53 to manage DNS and route traffic for their applications around the world, and our job is to make that easy, reliable, and fast. No two days look the same. You might start the morning extending the AI tooling that service teams across Route 53 use to build their own console changes, review a change one of those teams submitted and hold the bar on the console patterns and the design guidelines, then spend the afternoon on the health checking infrastructure itself, on the checkers that monitor millions of endpoints or the public API in front of them. Some days you go deep on a distributed system, other days you are building tooling or trying out a new AI tool. You review code, help decide what the team builds next, and partner with service teams across AWS networking to ship features that reach customers everywhere. When a hackathon idea grabs you, there is room to chase it.

About the team
We are a tight knit team that cares about our customers and about running a highly available platform on the Internet. We like to experiment and to learn out loud, whether that is a hackathon, a demo of something you just built, or a session digging into a new AI tool together. We are good at making sense of ambiguity and shipping products people rely on, and we welcome bold ideas and give you the ownership to take them all the way. And when we are not building, we make time to have fun together with regular team outings.

If you want to work on hard problems at scale and help decide where an AWS service goes next, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services' Cloud Storage, AWS S3, is one of the largest distributed storage systems in the world. Managing trillions of objects in storage, retrieving them in sub-x ms, building software that deploys to tens of thousands of hosts, building applications serving billions of transactions per second, achieving 99.999999999% (you didn’t read that wrong, that’s 11 nines!) durability. Amazon S3 powers businesses across the globe that make the lives of consumers better daily. As a Software Development Engineer in S3, you get to deliver these capabilities and delight our customers through teams of talented engineers and leaders.

With trillions of objects to manage, keeping track of what is stored on S3 is difficult. S3 Index develops the software responsible for durability and availability of key-value metadata. We tackle some of the hardest computer science problems. We build systems that can handle wildly varying client application access patterns and unprecedented loads by our customers. S3 Index responsively scales customer workloads, without the need for customers to provision capacity, is what puts the "Simple" in Simple Storage Service (S3).

S3 Index is looking for a passionate software engineer to build the next generation of S3 Index systems.

jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer, AWS ElastiCache
jobs.description:
This is an opportunity to join one of AWS's most foundational and high-impact engineering teams — the Data Plane team within Amazon ElastiCache and
MemoryDB. We own the core in-memory engine that powers millions of customer workloads: the data path, durability layer, replication protocol, snapshot
system, and advanced data structures. Our work sits at the intersection of systems programming, database internals, and performance engineering — every microsecond matters when you're serving the world's most latency-sensitive applications.

If you've ever found yourself deep in a conversation about write-ahead logs, copy-on-write fork semantics, lock-free data structures, or memory allocator design — and you want to apply those ideas to a system handling millions of operations per second at cloud scale — this team is where you belong. We build the engine behind Amazon MemoryDB, the only Valkey-compatible database that delivers in-memory speed with Multi-AZ durability. We're not just running an open-source cache; we're extending Valkey with novel capabilities — durable replication, active-active conflict resolution, full-text and vector search — while maintaining the sub-millisecond latencies our customers depend on.

Our customers include Disney+, Snap, Zoom, Lyft, Airbnb, and hundreds of thousands of other AWS customers who trust us with their most performance-critical workloads. You'll work in C/C++ at the lowest levels of the stack, solving problems in memory management, I/O optimization, replication protocols, and distributed data systems — all in production at massive scale.

Key job responsibilities
As a Software Development Engineer on the Data Plane team, you will take on broad ownership of the core engine that sits at the heart of ElastiCache and
MemoryDB. Your core responsibilities will include:

Designing and building the next-generation in-memory database engine, delivering sub-millisecond latencies and millions of operations per second to the world's most demanding applications.
Developing large-scale distributed in-memory storage systems in C/C++, extending open-source Valkey with durability, replication, and advanced data structure capabilities.
Building and optimizing the durability layer — transaction logging, snapshotting, and replication protocols — that enables MemoryDB to deliver in-memory speed with Multi-AZ data protection.
Designing and implementing advanced data structures and query capabilities including vector search and full-text search to support emerging workloads like generative AI.
Driving performance engineering at the systems level — memory allocator tuning, I/O path optimization, and lock-free concurrency — to push throughput and latency boundaries.
Contributing to active-active replication and conflict resolution mechanisms that enable globally distributed, low-latency data access.
Mentoring and growing engineers on the team, serving as a technical leader and role model for engineering best practices.

Managing individual project priorities, deadlines, and deliverables with a high degree of autonomy and accountability.

A day in the life
Day-to-day, you can expect a dynamic mix of deep technical work and collaborative engineering. A typical week might look like:

Writing and reviewing production-quality C/C++ code for the core in-memory engine — optimizing data structures, replication paths, and the durability layer for maximum throughput at minimal latency.
Participating in design reviews and architecture discussions, where you'll debate trade-offs around durability guarantees, memory efficiency, and replication consistency — and then go build the solution.
Collaborating with peer engineers to debug complex systems issues at the engine level - analyzing crash dumps, tracing memory corruption, and profiling hot paths under production-scale load.
Working with upstream open-source Valkey contributors and internal partner teams to integrate new capabilities and ensure our extensions remain compatible and performant.
Engaging with product teams to understand emerging customer needs — from generative AI workloads requiring vector search to globally distributed applications needing active-active replication — and translating those into engine capabilities.
Mentoring engineers through code reviews, design feedback, and pairing sessions, helping them grow their systems programming skills and engineering judgment.
Contributing to the team's operational excellence by participating in on-call rotations and driving improvements to engine reliability and diagnostic tooling.

About the team
The Data Plane team is a passionate group of engineers who thrive on solving hard problems at the intersection of database internals and distributed systems. We are a collaborative, intellectually curious team that values technical depth, ownership, and a bias for action. We own the core engine behind Amazon ElastiCache and MemoryDB — the in-memory data path, durability layer, replication protocol, and advanced query capabilities that hundreds of thousands of AWS customers depend on for their most latency-sensitive workloads.

Our customers include some of the world's fastest-growing startups and largest enterprises, all relying on our engine to deliver sub-millisecond performance at scale. We are deeply invested in open-source software and actively contribute to the Valkey community. As a team, we believe in growing together — senior engineers are directly involved in mentoring and developing engineers at all levels, and we take pride in building a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, WW Stores FinTech

A centerpiece of this work is MetricsEngine, a greenfield platform we are building from the ground up to become the single source of truth for financial metric computation across WWASFT.

MetricsEngine introduces a governed registry of metric definitions with versioning and ownership, a unified query layer that federates computation across multiple analytical backends, a single API surface for consistent consumption, and opt-in materialization for sub-second dashboard latency. Critically, MetricsEngine publishes its metric catalog to AI discovery and agent frameworks, enabling intelligent systems to reason over, compute, and surface financial insights using standardized definitions without human intervention.

You will own the design and delivery of key platform components end-to-end, contribute to architectural decisions that shape how the system scales, and write high-quality code that sets the standard for the team. You will collaborate closely with senior engineers and partner teams to solve ambiguous problems, influence technical direction through your implementations, and help establish patterns that the broader organization adopts.

If you enjoy solving complex technical challenges in high-data-volume environments, building foundational platforms from scratch, and making a tangible impact on Amazon's financial ecosystem worldwide, this role is your opportunity. Come join us on this exciting journey!

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build core components of MetricsEngine end-to-end: contribute to the governed metric registry, federated query layer, unified API, materialization framework, and AI-facing catalog that serves as the single source of financial truth across WWASFT products.
- Build the integration layer between MetricsEngine and AI agent frameworks, enabling intelligent systems to discover, interpret, and compute financial metrics programmatically using governed definitions.
- Design and implement scalable data infrastructure components, applying architectural patterns that optimize performance, security, and reliability across the data lifecycle from ingestion to reporting.
- Contribute to technical direction and team standards. Implement data access frameworks and storage patterns. Participate in design reviews and champion engineering best practices that elevate code quality and data integrity.
- Raise the bar for the team through code reviews, technical guidance, and knowledge sharing. Grow your expertise in distributed systems, cloud architecture, and system design while helping onboard and support fellow engineers.
- Partner with Software Engineers, Software Managers, Product Managers, Data Engineers, and cross-functional teams to deliver solutions that meet business objectives and technical requirements.

About the team
The Worldwide Amazon Stores Finance Technology (WWASFT) team is the dedicated technology partner for Amazon's global Amazon Stores (AS) organization. Our mission is to deliver innovative technical solutions that empower Amazon Stores' financial and operational processes and systems. We provide advanced, state-of-the-art tools and services to support over 4,000+ Finance end-users across all Consumer and Operations finance verticals. Our team owns and maintains a suite of centralized fintech products enabling critical financial activities, including planning, variance analysis, allocations, data management, analytics, reporting, and compliance and controllership functions. Through our work, we drive efficiency, accuracy, and strategic decision-making across Amazon's vast financial ecosystem.

Whether you're passionate about building highly scalable and reliable systems or a software developer who likes to solve business problems, Selling Partner Services (SPS) is the place for you. Our team is responsible for Case Management System.

We are looking for software engineers who thrive on complex problems and solve for operating complex and mission critical systems under high loads. Our systems manage case resolution systems with hundreds of millions of requests, and respond to millions of service requests. We have both frontend and backend code stack and opportunities.
